Uses \"URL alias\" | `slug` front matter | `slug` front matter, `:slug` placeholder |\n| Draft / published | `post_status` | Published / Unpublished flag | `draft: true` | `_drafts/` folder or `published: false` |\n| Role | Administrator, Editor, Author, Contributor, Subscriber | User-defined roles. Standard: anonymous, authenticated, administrator | Not found (no users) | Not found (no users) |\n| Capability / permission | \"Capability\", e.g. `publish_posts` | \"Permission\", granted to roles | Not found | Not found |\n| Permalink | The permanent URL of an item | Not found as a term | Absolute URL including scheme and host | The output path |\n| Taxonomy | Categories, tags, custom taxonomies | Vocabularies of terms | Taxonomies of terms (config) | Categories and tags (no custom taxonomies found) |\n| Theme | Design of the site | Files for look and feel | Module with layout and behavior | Gem or folder of layouts, includes, assets |\n| Headless | Term not found in the pages I read | \"Decoupled\" / \"headless\" docs exist but are thin | Different meaning: \"headless bundle\" | Not found |\n\n## 3. WordPress\n\n**Content type.** WordPress calls this a \"post type\". The built-in ones are `post`, `page`, `attachment`, `revision` and nav menu items. Developers can register custom post types. They are stored in the same `posts` table. Sources: https://developer.wordpress.org/plugins/post-types/registering-custom-post-types/ and https://developer.wordpress.org/plugins/post-types/\n\n**Slug.** The REST API describes it as \"An alphanumeric identifier for the post unique to its type.\" Source: https://developer.wordpress.org/rest-api/reference/posts/. The `%postname%` tag turns \"This Is A Great Post!\" into `this-is-a-great-post`. Source: https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/customize-permalinks/. The slug function limits output to letters, digits, underscore and dash. Source: https://developer.wordpress.org/reference/functions/sanitize_title/. I did not verify how it treats Chinese characters.\n\n**Post status.** There are 8 built-in statuses: publish, future, draft, pending, private, trash, auto-draft, inherit. Source: https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/post-status/. Key facts:\n- `publish`: \"Viewable by everyone.\"\n- `draft`: incomplete post.\n- `pending`: \"Awaiting a user with the `publish_posts` capability (typically a user assigned the Editor role) to publish.\"\n- A user with `edit_posts` but not `publish_posts` sees a \"Submit for Review\" button instead of \"Publish\". The post gets the `pending` status.\n\n**Role.** \"A Role defines a set of tasks a user assigned the role is allowed to perform.\" The docs add: \"One particular role should not be considered to be senior to another role.\" Source: https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/roles-and-capabilities/. Default roles from the same page:\n- Administrator: access to all admin features on one site.\n- Editor: \"can publish and manage posts including the posts of other users.\"\n- Author: \"can publish and manage their own posts.\"\n- Contributor: \"can write and manage their own posts but cannot publish them.\"\n- Subscriber: \"can only manage their profile.\"\n\n**Capability.** A role is a set of capabilities, such as `publish_posts`. Capabilities can be added or removed with `add_cap()` and `remove_cap()`. Source: same roles page. Its capability table shows:\n- Contributor has `edit_posts` and `delete_posts`. It does not have `publish_posts`.\n- Author has `publish_posts` and `upload_files`.\n- Editor also has `edit_others_posts`, `edit_pages` and `publish_pages`.\n\n**Permalink.** \"Permalinks are the permanent URLs of your posts, pages, categories, and other archive pages.\" The default \"Plain\" form is `?p=N`. \"Pretty\" forms use the post name. Source: https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/customize-permalinks/\n\n**Taxonomy.** Source: https://developer.wordpress.org/plugins/taxonomies/ and https://developer.wordpress.org/plugins/taxonomies/working-with-custom-taxonomies/\n- A taxonomy is a way to group things. It can be hierarchical or flat.\n- Built-in: Categories (hierarchical) and Tags (flat).\n- Custom taxonomies are registered with `register_taxonomy`.\n- Category and tag archive URLs use a \"base\" prefix (`/category/name`, `/tag/name`). The default bases are `category` and `tag`. Source: https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/customize-permalinks/\n\n**Theme.** \"A WordPress theme represents the design of your website.\" Block themes and classic (PHP) themes exist. Source: https://developer.wordpress.org/themes/getting-started/what-is-a-theme/\n\n**Headless.** The REST API lets you \"bring your WordPress content into completely separate applications.\" Source: https://developer.wordpress.org/rest-api/. The word \"headless\" did not appear in that page. I found no official definition.\n\n## 4. Drupal\n\n**Content type.** A content entity is \"An item of content data...\" A content entity type groups entities with different purposes. A bundle (content type) is a subtype with smaller variations. A field is a \"storage unit\" holding one kind of data. Source: https://www.drupal.org/docs/user_guide/en/planning-data-types.html. The User Guide builds example types called Vendor and Recipe. Source: https://www.drupal.org/docs/user_guide/en/structure-content-type.html\n\n**Slug and permalink.** Neither word is used. Drupal has a \"path\" (the last part of a URL, like `node/7`) and a \"URL alias\" that gives it a friendlier name. Source: https://www.drupal.org/docs/user_guide/en/content-paths.html\n\n**Published / unpublished.** \"The Content item entity type supports marking each content item as either Published or Unpublished.\" Permissions differ by state. The core Workflows module adds more states. Content Moderation lets you give roles permission to specific transitions. Source: https://www.drupal.org/docs/user_guide/en/planning-workflow.html\n\n**Role and permission.** A permission is the ability to do one action. Permissions are grouped into roles. Users can have several roles. Standard roles: Anonymous, Authenticated, and Administrator (created at install, gets all permissions). Source: https://www.drupal.org/docs/user_guide/en/user-concept.html. Drupal says \"permission\" where WordPress says \"capability\".\n\n**Taxonomy.** A vocabulary is a set of terms, such as \"the set of all blog post tags.\" Terms attach to content through reference fields. Authors can either create terms freely or pick from a fixed list. Source: https://www.drupal.org/docs/user_guide/en/structure-taxonomy.html\n\n**Theme.** \"A theme is a set of files that define the visual look and feel of your site.\" Source: https://www.drupal.org/docs/user_guide/en/understanding-themes.html\n\n**Headless.** Drupal has a \"Decoupled Drupal\" doc section. The \"What is decoupled\" page is marked \"needs work\" and gives no clear definition. Its outline says the backend \"only exposes content via an API\". Source: https://www.drupal.org/docs/develop/decoupled-drupal/what-is-decoupled. The core JSON:API module gives \"RESTful CRUD for a Drupal site's content.\" Source: https://www.drupal.org/docs/core-modules-and-themes/core-modules/jsonapi-module\n\n## 5. Hugo\n\n**Content type.** \"A classification of content inferred from the top-level directory name or the `type` set in front matter.\" Source: https://gohugo.io/getting-started/glossary/. A page in `content/posts/` is in the `posts` section. Source: https://gohugo.io/content-management/organization/\n\n**Slug and URL.** By default the URL matches the file path. The `slug` field changes the last segment. The `url` field replaces the whole path. The `permalinks` setting can build URLs from tokens like `:section` and `:slug`. Source: https://gohugo.io/content-management/urls/ and https://gohugo.io/content-management/front-matter/\n\n**Draft / published.** `draft` stops rendering unless you pass `--buildDrafts`. `publishDate` in the future also stops rendering. `expiryDate` stops it after a date. Source: https://gohugo.io/content-management/front-matter/. The glossary has no entry for \"draft\".\n\n**Permalink.** The glossary calls it \"The absolute URL of a published resource or a rendered page, including scheme and host.\" Source: https://gohugo.io/getting-started/glossary/. Note: this differs from WordPress, where a permalink is a stable URL. It also differs from our relative-path rule. Hugo has a `relativeURLs` setting, but the docs describe it as useful only for serverless sites. Source: https://gohugo.io/content-management/urls/\n\n**Taxonomy.** \"Taxonomies are classifications of logical relationships between content.\" Parts: taxonomy, term, value. Source: https://gohugo.io/content-management/taxonomies/\n- Defaults are `tags` and `categories`. Config maps singular to plural, such as `category: categories`. Source: https://gohugo.io/configuration/taxonomies/\n- You add terms in front matter, using the plural name.\n- Hugo builds a list page of all terms and one page per term. Templates are `taxonomy.html` and `term.html`. Source: https://gohugo.io/templates/taxonomy/\n- The docs I read show `author: author` as a custom example. Source: https://gohugo.io/configuration/taxonomies/\n\n**Menus.** A page joins a menu with `menus: main` in front matter. Source: https://gohugo.io/content-management/menus/\n\n**Theme.** \"A module that delivers a complete set of components defining a site's layout, presentation, and behavior.\" Source: https://gohugo.io/getting-started/glossary/\n\n**Roles.** Not found. Hugo has no users. Who can publish is decided by who can commit to the repo. That last part is my inference, not a quote.\n\n**Headless.** In Hugo, \"headless\" means \"headless bundles\": unpublished pages whose content is reused in other pages. This is not a headless CMS. Source: https://gohugo.io/content-management/build-options/. The glossary has no \"headless CMS\" entry.\n\n## 6. Jekyll\n\n**Content type.** Posts live in `_posts` and are named `YEAR-MONTH-DAY-title.MARKUP`. Source: https://jekyllrb.com/docs/posts/. Pages are for \"standalone content (content which is not date based...)\". Source: https://jekyllrb.com/docs/pages/. Collections group other content. Posts are a built-in collection. Source: https://jekyllrb.com/docs/collections/\n\n**Slug and permalink.** \"Permalinks are the output path for your pages, posts, or collections.\" `:title` comes from the filename. `:slug` replaces non-alphanumerics with hyphens and lowercases. The `slug` front matter field overrides `:title`. Source: https://jekyllrb.com/docs/permalinks/\n\n**Draft / published.** Drafts are \"unpublished posts\" kept in `_drafts/`. Source: https://jekyllrb.com/docs/structure/. `published: false` hides a post. Preview it with `--unpublished`. Source: https://jekyllrb.com/docs/front-matter/\n\n**Taxonomy.** Posts have `categories` and `tags`. Categories can also come from the folder path above `_posts`. Categories can appear in the URL. Tags cannot. Source: https://jekyllrb.com/docs/posts/. `site.tags.TAG` lists the posts with a tag. Source: https://jekyllrb.com/docs/variables/. I found no built-in per-tag or per-category pages. You write them by hand or with a plugin (not verified in the docs).\n\n**Theme.** Jekyll themes \"package up assets, layouts, includes, and stylesheets in a way that can be overridden by your site's content.\" Source: https://jekyllrb.com/docs/themes/\n\n**Roles and headless.** Not found.\n\n**Eleventy note.** Tags in front matter create collections. Pagination can make one page per item, for example one per tag, using a `permalink` template. Sources: https://www.11ty.dev/docs/collections/ and https://www.11ty.dev/docs/pagination/\n\n## 7. What this means for our project\n\nThese are suggestions, not decisions.\n\n- **Borrow WordPress's status split.** Use `draft`, `pending`, `published`. WordPress's `pending` means \"awaiting a user with the `publish_posts` capability\". That matches the client's \"admin reviews editor guides\" flow.\n- **Use two or three capabilities, not role checks everywhere.** For example `edit_own`, `edit_any`, `publish`. Roles are bundles of these. WordPress does it this way, and Drupal does it the same way with \"permissions\". Editor gets the first, admin gets all three. Route code checks the capability. Then the rule can change without touching routes.\n- **Treat our \"editor\" like WordPress's Contributor, not WordPress's Editor.** In WordPress, Contributor can write but \"cannot publish\" their posts, and WordPress Editor can publish others' posts. Our editor is closer to a Contributor.\n- **Hero and author as taxonomies.** Hugo's model fits: a taxonomy (`hero`, `author`) has terms, and content is assigned to terms. Hugo builds one list page per term and a terms index. Our `cms publish` could do the same with Jinja: loop over each hero and write `heroes/<slug>/index.html` with its published guides. Hugo's templates are `taxonomy.html` and `term.html`. WordPress and Drupal have the same idea (terms, vocabularies).\n- **Author may not need to be a taxonomy table.** It is already a user relation. A per-author list page can come from the `author` column. Hero can be a small table with a slug and a Chinese display name. Both give the same output page shape.\n- **Slugs must be decided early.** All four systems derive a slug from a title and use it in the URL. The WordPress slug function keeps only letters, digits, underscore and dash. I did not verify what happens to Chinese titles. For a Chinese-speaking audience, consider that a slug is typed or edited by the writer, ASCII or pinyin, and unique per type. This is a design risk to test, not a documented answer.\n- **Keep paths relative.** Hugo's \"permalink\" is absolute by definition, and its relative mode is described as niche. Our hard rule (no `href=\"/...\"`) means we compute relative paths ourselves, depending on page depth. Per-term pages like `heroes/<slug>/` are one level deeper than the home page.\n- **Patch version field.** None of the systems has a built-in \"patch version\". It is just a custom field: Drupal fields, WordPress custom fields/post meta, Hugo front matter. A plain `patch_version` column on posts, shown on the page and used to flag stale guides, matches what the others do. Hugo's `expiryDate` is a related idea (stop rendering after a date), but a patch version fits balance patches better. That comparison is my own.\n- **Navigation from published pages.** Hugo adds a page to a menu with `menus: main` in front matter. We could use a `show_in_nav` flag on pages, with the public nav built only from published rows.\n- **Headless is optional.** A static export is a stronger form of decoupling than a headless API. Our admin is the content backend and the site is a build output. We do not need a public API.\n\n## 8. Gaps\n\n- Drupal: no \"slug\", \"permalink\" or \"content editor\" role definition found. Drupal's theme page on `drupal.org` redirects in some docs paths, so I used the User Guide URL that returned content.\n- WordPress: no official definition of \"headless\" found.\n- Hugo and Jekyll: no definition of roles or capabilities found, and none of \"headless CMS\".\n- Jekyll: whether it can build per-term pages without a plugin is not stated on the pages I read.\n- Chinese-character slug behavior: not verified for any system.\n","numLines":145,"startLine":1,"totalLines":145}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"293c6999-f4c7-4199-9d58-2b43cb9a6fc1","session_id":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"d1e69fc1-c6bd-41bf-a746-f18c4278d904","version":"2.1.288","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}

Students have two weeks and no\nhosting budget, and a first web application with real authentication is an\nattractive target the moment it is public.\n\n## Decision\n\nThe admin console (FastAPI + SQLite) runs on the student's own machine. A\n`cms publish` step renders the published content to static HTML in `site/`, which\nis deployed to GitHub Pages on the `gh-pages` branch.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Login, roles, and the database are never exposed to the internet.\n- The public site cannot have server-side features (search, comments) without a\n  different host; a stretch goal may add a live admin deploy behind a security gate.\n- Publishing is explicit: content changes are not live until `cms publish` runs,\n  which is a behaviour worth documenting for your client.\n- Relative paths become mandatory, because Pages serves the site from a subfolder.\n\n## Why this is an ADR\n\nIt is hard to reverse (it shapes every route, template, and deploy step) and it\nis surprising without context (most CMSes are servers). Options\nconsidered: Django (batteries included, but a large amount of generated code to\nread), Flask (similar to FastAPI here), a JavaScript stack (a second language and\na build step), and FastAPI with server-rendered templates.\n\n## Decision\n\nFastAPI with Jinja2 templates, SQLite for storage, argon2 for password hashing,\nand an HTML sanitizer for user Markdown. {"parentUuid":"65e48f9c-6a0f-4a58-a03f-08343c4b27d7","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"9866ebf7-c4bb-4fdd-a5c1-dbb3a627c9bf","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01MWzZK67bUmVxdc6SQ8CeCA","type":"tool_result","content":"261\t## Part 3 — Your client\n262\t\n263\t**Time: 20 min.**\n264\t\n265\tYou are not building \"a CMS\". You are building one for someone, because specific people make specific demands, and those demands are what make your project yours.\n266\t\n267\t### 3.1 Pick a client\n268\t\n269\tChoose a real or plausible one you know something about: a club you belong to, a lab, a band, a campus office, a family business, a team. You will not contact them; you just need their reality.\n270\t\n271\t**If nothing comes to mind**, use the default:\n272\t\n273\t> **Knox County Historical Society.** Three volunteers run the site. Karen, the secretary, posts meeting announcements and event notices weekly; she is comfortable with email and nothing more. Tom, the president, writes longer research pieces every month or two and wants them to look permanent. Nobody should be able to edit the membership page except Tom. Their current site is a Facebook page they cannot search, and members ask them the same three questions every month: when is the next meeting, where is it, and what is on the agenda.\n274\t\n275\tIf you take the default, add **at least three details of your own** — a person, a constraint, a recurring frustration. Generic input produces a generic project, and that costs points under factor A.\n276\t\n277\t### 3.2 Write the brief\n278\t\n279\tCreate `notes/client-brief.md`. Half a page, in your words:\n280\t\n281\t- Who runs the site, and how comfortable are they with computers?\n282\t- Who reads it, and what are they usually trying to find?\n283\t- What is broken about how they do it now?\n284\t- What would make them say \"this is better\"?\n285\t- What must **not** happen? (e.g. \"a volunteer must never be able to delete the members page\")\n286\t\n287\t### 3.3 The required capabilities\n288\t\n289\tYour CMS can name things however your client would. Underneath, all seven of these must work. This list is fixed; how you get there is yours.\n290\t\n291\t1. **Login** — admins and editors sign in and out; passwords are stored hashed, never as text.\n292\t2. **Two roles** — *admin* and *editor*, with genuinely different permissions.\n293\t3. **Posts** — create, read, update, delete; title, slug, Markdown body, draft/published, author, timestamps.\n294\t4. **Pages** — same, and published pages appear in the public navigation.\n295\t5. **Admin console** — dashboard with counts, a content list you can filter, an editor with a preview.\n296\t6. **User management** — admin only: create users, change roles, deactivate; a deactivated user cannot log in.\n297\t7. **Public site and publish** — only published content, Markdown sanitized, nav built from pages, `cms publish` writes `site/` with relative paths.\n298\t\n299\t**Deliberately excluded** (do not build these): multi-site, drag-and-drop page builders, rich-text WYSIWYG editors. They cost far more than they teach.\n300\t\n301\t---\n302\t\n303\t## Part 4 — Exercise A: the context-threshold hook\n304\t\n305\t**Time: 30 min.** Full instructions: `docs/mp2-setup_context-threshold-hook_20260922.md` in your repo. Summary:"}]},"uuid":"3a74e7ca-7792-43fb-acd6-543d6b486e8d","timestamp":"2026-10-16T14:37:23.224Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2/docs/manual_iphs400_mp2-web-cms_20260922.md","content":"## Part 3 — Your client\n\n**Time: 20 min.**\n\nYou are not building \"a CMS\". You are building one for someone, because specific people make specific demands, and those demands are what make your project yours.\n\n### 3.1 Pick a client\n\nChoose a real or plausible one you know something about: a club you belong to, a lab, a band, a campus office, a family business, a team. You will not contact them; you just need their reality.\n\n**If nothing comes to mind**, use the default:\n\n> **Knox County Historical Society.** Three volunteers run the site. Karen, the secretary, posts meeting announcements and event notices weekly; she is comfortable with email and nothing more. Tom, the president, writes longer research pieces every month or two and wants them to look permanent. Nobody should be able to edit the membership page except Tom. Their current site is a Facebook page they cannot search, and members ask them the same three questions every month: when is the next meeting, where is it, and what is on the agenda.\n\nIf you take the default, add **at least three details of your own** — a person, a constraint, a recurring frustration. Generic input produces a generic project, and that costs points under factor A.\n\n### 3.2 Write the brief\n\nCreate `notes/client-brief.md`. Half a page, in your words:\n\n- Who runs the site, and how comfortable are they with computers?\n- Who reads it, and what are they usually trying to find?\n- What is broken about how they do it now?\n- What would make them say \"this is better\"?\n- What must **not** happen? (e.g. \"a volunteer must never be able to delete the members page\")\n\n### 3.3 The required capabilities\n\nYour CMS can name things however your client would. Underneath, all seven of these must work. This list is fixed; how you get there is yours.\n\n1. **Login** — admins and editors sign in and out; passwords are stored hashed, never as text.\n2. **Two roles** — *admin* and *editor*, with genuinely different permissions.\n3. **Posts** — create, read, update, delete; title, slug, Markdown body, draft/published, author, timestamps.\n4. **Pages** — same, and published pages appear in the public navigation.\n5. **Admin console** — dashboard with counts, a content list you can filter, an editor with a preview.\n6. **User management** — admin only: create users, change roles, deactivate; a deactivated user cannot log in.\n7. **Public site and publish** — only published content, Markdown sanitized, nav built from pages, `cms publish` writes `site/` with relative paths.\n\n**Deliberately excluded** (do not build these): multi-site, drag-and-drop page builders, rich-text WYSIWYG editors. They cost far more than they teach.\n\n---\n\n## Part 4 — Exercise A: the context-threshold hook\n\n**Time: 30 min.** Full instructions: `docs/mp2-setup_context-threshold-hook_20260922.md` in your repo. {"parentUuid":"390a1f06-b0b9-4522-95ea-22c1237daa52","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg65vW6mMzLgpez6ozViJ","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I've read the brief, field notes, research, the manual's Part 3.3, and both ADRs, and set `.claude/state/phase` to `grill`. Some things in the brief still need deciding. The questions below don't depend on each other, so you can answer them in any order.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q1** - **What is a \"post\" here?** Capability 3 requires posts. In your brief, every piece of written content an editor makes is a **guide (攻略)**. Can a post be anything other than a guide? For example: a patch-notes summary, an announcement from a streamer, or a tournament recap.\n\n- (a) Post = Guide, with only one kind. Every post has a hero and a patch.\n- (b) Posts have a kind: guide / news / ...\n\n➡️ (a). Call it **Guide** everywhere and put \"Post\" under _Avoid_. The brief only describes guides, and adding a second kind doubles the browse logic for no clear client need. News can stay on Bilibili, like comments.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q2** - **What are Tournaments (锦标赛)?** The menu has Guides, Tournaments and About. Capability 4 says pages show up in the public nav. Is Tournaments:\n\n- (a) a single **Page** an admin writes and updates by hand (upcoming events, sign-up links, past winners), like About; or\n- (b) its own list of tournament entries, which would be a second content type with dates and results?\n\n➡️ (a). Tournaments and About are both **Pages**, written by admins only. Guides is a generated list in the nav, not a Page. If (b) is what the community really needs, it's a whole new content type and should probably be cut from the two-week scope.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q3** - **How is a guide tied to a hero?** The Bazaar has a fixed roster of heroes (Vanessa, Pygmalien, Dooley, Mak, Stelle, Jules, …), and new ones arrive with updates. A few decisions are bundled here:\n\n- Who maintains the hero list: admins in the console, or editors typing a free-text hero name on each guide? Free text produces \"瓦妮莎\", \"Vanessa\" and \"vanessa\" as three separate heroes.\n- How many heroes per guide: exactly one, or zero or one (for general guides like economy or item tier lists), or several?\n\n➡️ Admins maintain the **Hero** list (Chinese display name plus an ASCII slug for the URL). Each guide has **zero or one** hero, and guides with no hero go under a \"通用 / General\" bucket. The brief's main search is \"a guide for a specific hero on a specific patch\", so one hero per guide keeps that browse clean.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q4** - **How does the site deal with balance patches?** This is the brief's biggest pain point (\"hard to say how much it still applies\"), but none of the 7 capabilities covers it. Options:\n\n- (a) Nothing. Readers judge freshness from the publish date.\n- (b) Each guide records the **Patch** it was written for. Readers see it, and they can tell for themselves if it's old.\n- (c) Same as (b), plus admins set a **Current Patch**. Any published guide on an older patch gets an \"可能已过时 / may be outdated\" label on the public site.\n\n➡️ (c). It's cheap (a field plus one admin setting) and it fixes the problem you actually described. When a patch drops, the streamers update one setting instead of re-tagging every guide.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q5** - **What are the guide statuses?** The brief says an editor's guide \"stays a draft until an admin checks it and publishes it.\" That uses \"draft\" for two different states: unfinished, and finished but waiting for review. Your research suggests WordPress's split:\n\n- **Draft**: the author is still writing. Admins can ignore it.\n- **Submitted (待审核)**: the editor says it's done. It shows up in the admin's review queue.\n- **Published**: live on the next `cms publish`.\n\nOr keep just draft/published (the minimum for capability 3), and admins find guides to review by scanning every editor draft.\n\n➡️ Three statuses. Your client admins are streamers who are \"not very comfortable with computers\", so a \"待审核 (N)\" count on the dashboard is the difference between reviews happening and not happening. Editors move Draft → Submitted. Only admins move anything to Published. Questions about what happens next (sending a guide back, editing after publishing) wait for round 2.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q6** - **What language do the site and the console use?** The readers, writers and admins are all Chinese speakers.\n\n➡️ The public site and the admin console both use Simplified Chinese for every label. Code, tickets and `CONTEXT.md` use English terms, with each glossary entry listing its Chinese label (Guide = 攻略, Hero = 英雄, Patch = 版本). That way the vocabulary stays one-to-one across both languages."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1979,"cache_read_input_tokens":57253,"output_tokens":3153,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":1548},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1979,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":3153,"cache_read_input_tokens":57253,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1979,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1979},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011Cg65vVnv154mL4vHh5bLY","attributionSkill":"mattpocock-skills:domain-modeling","attributionPlugin":"mattpocock-skills","type":"assistant","uuid":"c306ebf7-38a6-4160-a3ed-79aed7eb7c92","timestamp":"2026-10-16T14:37:59.681Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"high","perTurnEffort":"high","session_id":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"d1e69fc1-c6bd-41bf-a746-f18c4278d904","version":"2.1.288","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}

{"type":"file-history-snapshot","messageId":"838860c8-a958-43bb-bb8c-7908d8622149","snapshot":{"messageId":"838860c8-a958-43bb-bb8c-7908d8622149","trackedFileBackups":{},"timestamp":"2026-10-16T14:58:27.116Z"},"isSnapshotUpdate":false}
{"parentUuid":"a2bf1852-9052-402c-b2a1-426eb9ef3ac8","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"78e9ff3f-4216-4067-8570-d954f71af5f8","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":"for question one, post I imagine for now is mainly guide. Idealy each will include several screenshots or further edited images that shows for example the lineup or the deck of each game with scrips explanation of it. Because there are other websites that do well like a wikipedia of the game (you can consider the example of wiki.52poke.com for pokemon)that will includes cards information and patch notes, so that will not be the focus, but you are right that it is also worth putting on the website. announcement from a streamer won't be necessary, but it is ok to be put on. Tournament recap is also a good suggestion, that you can put into the tournament section. \nfor question two, tournament is a new mode of the game that is currently being tested, basically for traditional games, each player play on their own and their opponents are mirror players, and in the tournament, multiple (can up to 50 or even 100)players play at the same time in one game and will have a champion in the end. The reason why I wish to have these separate sections for guide on the top of the web page is that I try to organize different type of information. About is just a page to show for example who is running the website, where to contact, etc.\nfor question three, I guess it is better that each guide only has one hero involved, edtitors can decide which heros they are giving guides on when they write each post because this is pretty straight forward, and admins can have the power to make adjustments if any guide is mistakenly put in the wrong hero's section. Also this remind me that it is also better to let the edtior also indicates what the version of the game they are giving guides on, for example, 6.7, because after each patch, the environment of the game will be totally different and version of the game is another straight forward and important information.\nfor question four, I think I have covered this in question three, I guess b makes sense to me, the problem of option c is that because patch nerfs happens so often and it takes time to finish guides, it is possible that someone posts some guides that are for the previous version, and if none of the cards in the guide is changed, then it is still useful, but in fact it is not current version.\nfor question five, I think you are using draft for two different things. If a post is unfinished, I guess it is a draft that idealy the web will save for the editors to come back later. When an editor finishes the post and hit the publish button, then it becomes a post that is ready for the admin to review that is shown on their ends, this is a different status, and when the admin approves it, it is officially published.\nfor question 6, currently it is designed for only Chinese readers, but as the game is originally in English and has a lot of players who speaks English, it also makes sense to have two languages that users can switch between. The For heros, skills, and cards, there are official game name in both Chinese and English, while for other parts of the guide, I guess a machine translate will be fine, maybe AI involed, which is more humanized. If possible, the editor can choose to upload any languages of the guide (between English and Chinese) or even both of them."},"uuid":"838860c8-a958-43bb-bb8c-7908d8622149","timestamp":"2026-10-16T14:58:27.065Z","permissionMode":"bypassPermissions","origin":{"kind":"human"},"promptSource":"typed","turnOrigin":"human","turnPosition":{"promptIndex":2,"turnIndex":2},"userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"d1e69fc1-c6bd-41bf-a746-f18c4278d904","version":"2.1.288","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}

{"parentUuid":"7536681c-1341-4d5e-b06c-a119c9520861","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg67bDVqb6GXEF9JbyTC4","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01X3i3m3hVWMM6WNrQhFzxi2","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2/CONTEXT.md","content":"# The Bazaar Guide Site (大巴扎攻略站)\n\nA small CMS where streamers (up主) and invited writers in the Chinese-speaking\ncommunity of the card game The Bazaar publish written guides, so players can\nfind a build for a given hero and patch without scrubbing through videos.\n\n## Language\n\n### People\n\n**Admin** (管理员):\nOne of the few top streamers who run the site. Reviews and publishes other\npeople's Guides and manages users.\n_Avoid_: owner, superuser\n\n**Editor** (编辑):\nAn invited guide writer (another up主 or an experienced player). Writes\nGuides but cannot publish them or manage users.\n_Avoid_: author (as a role name), contributor, writer\n\n**Reader** (读者):\nAnyone who plays the game and reads the public site. Has no account.\n_Avoid_: user, visitor, member\n\n### Content\n\n**Guide** (攻略):\nA written strategy piece about one Hero on one Patch, typically built around\nscreenshots of a lineup or deck with an explanation of how it plays.\n_Avoid_: article, tutorial\n\n**Hero** (英雄):\nA playable character in The Bazaar, with an official Chinese and English name.\nEvery Guide is about exactly one Hero.\n_Avoid_: character, class\n\n**Patch** (版本):\nThe game version a Guide was written for, such as `6.7`. Stated by the\nwriter. It describes when the Guide was written and is not a verdict on\nwhether the Guide is out of date.\n_Avoid_: version (also used for edits to a Guide), season\n\n**Page** (页面):\nA standalone piece of site content written by an Admin, such as About (关于),\nthat appears in the public navigation.\n_Avoid_: static page\n\n### Workflow\n\n**Draft** (草稿):\nA Guide its writer has not finished yet. Only its writer and Admins can see it.\n_Avoid_: unpublished\n\n**Submitted** (待审核):\nA Guide its writer has marked finished, waiting for an Admin to review it.\n_Avoid_: pending, draft, ready\n\n**Published** (已发布):\nA Guide an Admin has approved. It is eligible to appear on the public site.\n_Avoid_: live, approved\n\n## Flagged ambiguities\n\n- \"Draft\" was being used for both an unfinished Guide and a finished one\n  awaiting review. Those are now **Draft** and **Submitted**.\n- \"Version\" can mean the game's Patch or an edit to a Guide. Use **Patch** for\n  the game.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":4704,"cache_read_input_tokens":63304,"output_tokens":1024,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":54},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":4704,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1024,"cache_read_input_tokens":63304,"cache_creation_input_tokens":4704,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":4704},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01X3i3m3hVWMM6WNrQhFzxi2":{"file_path":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2/CONTEXT.md","content":"# The Bazaar Guide Site (大巴扎攻略站)\n\nA small CMS where streamers (up主) and invited writers in the Chinese-speaking\ncommunity of the card game The Bazaar publish written guides, so players can\nfind a build for a given hero and patch without scrubbing through videos.\n\n## Language\n\n### People\n\n**Admin** (管理员):\nOne of the few top streamers who run the site. {"parentUuid":"ec3572d8-22a1-4439-84be-95a3174f5eb4","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg67bwvFP2vpo9G9NQm7R","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I've added your answers to `CONTEXT.md`: Admin, Editor, Reader, Guide, Hero, Patch, Page, and the three statuses Draft → Submitted → Published. I picked up four points from what you wrote. You chose (b) on patches: the writer states the Patch, and the site doesn't judge whether it's stale. Tournaments is a section of content, not a Page. About is a Page. And bilingual support is a real requirement. Round 2:\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q1** - **What goes in the Tournaments section?** Tournament mode has many players in one game and a single champion. Two kinds of content would sit under 锦标赛:\n\n- **Tournament strategy guides**: still about a Hero and a Patch, but for tournament mode.\n- **Tournament recaps**: who won and what builds placed. These usually aren't tied to one Hero.\n\nSo does a Guide carry a **Mode** (标准 / 锦标赛), with recaps as a separate kind of post? Or is everything under 锦标赛 just \"tournament posts\" with an optional hero?\n\n➡️ Every Guide has a **Mode**: Standard or Tournament. The **Guides** menu lists Standard-mode Guides by Hero and Author. The **Tournaments** menu lists Tournament-mode Guides by Hero, plus **Recaps**. A Recap is a second, simpler kind of post with a Patch but no Hero, and only Admins write it. I'd leave streamer announcements out of v1, since you said they aren't necessary.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q2** - **Do editors pick the Hero from a list or type it?** You said editors choose the hero and admins fix mistakes. If editors type it freely, \"瓦妮莎\", \"Vanessa\" and \"vanessa \" become three different Hero sections on the public site, and admins clean up after every guide.\n\n➡️ Admins maintain the Hero list (official Chinese name, English name, and a URL slug like `vanessa`). Editors pick from a dropdown. Admins can change any Guide's Hero. A new hero arriving in an update is a one-minute admin task.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q3** - **Is the Patch typed or picked?** It's the same problem: free text gives you `6.7`, `v6.7`, `6.7版本`, `6.70`. Readers will want to see \"Vanessa guides, newest patch first\", which only works if patches compare cleanly.\n\n➡️ Admins keep a short **Patch list** (`6.7`, `6.8`, …), and editors pick one, defaulting to the newest. On each Hero's page the public site groups Guides by Patch, newest first. Following your Q4 answer, older guides get no \"outdated\" label.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q4** - **How do images get into a guide?** Images are the core of a guide (lineups, decks), but none of the 7 capabilities covers uploads. Options:\n\n- (a) Writers host images elsewhere and paste the links into Markdown. This is free to build, but **Bilibili and many Chinese image hosts block hotlinking**, so images might show in the editor's preview and break on GitHub Pages. Streamers also won't be able to debug it.\n- (b) The admin console has an **image upload**. Files are stored locally, copied into `site/` on publish, and referenced by relative paths. `python-multipart` is already in the stack, so no new dependency is needed. Only PNG, JPG, WebP and GIF are accepted (SVG can carry scripts), with a size limit.\n- (c) Both.\n\n➡️ (b). This is the one feature your client can't do without, and (a) fails silently on exactly the hosts your writers use. It adds work beyond the 7 capabilities, so I'll make it its own ticket.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q5** - **What happens when an admin doesn't approve a guide?** The brief only covers approval. If the guide has a wrong build, a wrong hero, or isn't finished, what then?\n\n➡️ The admin **returns** it (退回) to Draft with a short note that the editor sees on the guide (\"配图缺失，请补充\"). The editor fixes it and submits again. Admins can also just fix small things themselves and publish.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q6** - **Can an editor change a guide after it's Published?** Your brief says an editor must never get unreviewed content onto the site. But typos happen, and so does \"card X got nerfed, here's the fix\". Options:\n\n- (a) Editors can't edit their Published guides. They ask an admin to make the change.\n- (b) An editor's edit sends the guide back to **Submitted**, and it drops off the public site at the next publish until an admin re-approves it.\n- (c) The live version stays up while the edited copy waits for review. This needs stored revisions, which is much more work.\n\nThere's also a related question: when patch 6.8 lands, does an author **update** their 6.7 guide, or **write a new 6.8 guide** and leave the 6.7 one as history?\n\n➡️ (b), plus \"new patch means a new Guide\". A Guide's Patch is part of what it *is*, so a 6.8 rewrite is a new Guide and the 6.7 one stays as an honest record. Post-publish edits are then just small fixes, and a short trip back through review is acceptable.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q7** - **\"Publish\" means two different things.** (1) An admin approves a Submitted guide, which makes it **Published**. (2) `cms publish` regenerates `site/` and pushes it to GitHub Pages (ADR-001). Neither is live until (2) runs. A streamer who clicks \"发布\" and refreshes the site will think it's broken. Also, you said the editor \"hits the publish button\", but an editor's button doesn't publish anything.\n\n➡️ Keep **Publish** for the admin's approval. Call the export step the **site build** (更新网站) in the glossary and the UI. The command stays `cms publish` because the assignment fixes that name. The dashboard shows \"N changes not yet on the site\". The editor's button is always **提交审核 (Submit)** and never says 发布.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q8** - **How far does bilingual support go?** This is the biggest scope question. A full bilingual site with AI translation would need a translation API, an API key, and a new dependency. It would also likely mistranslate card and skill names, which are exactly the terms that matter. That alone could use the whole two weeks. Options:\n\n- (a) Chinese only in v1. Hero names are stored in both languages so that English can be added later.\n- (b) Each Guide has a Chinese body and/or an English body (at least one), written by the author. They can paste in their own AI translation, as your brief already assumes for Markdown. A Guide page shows a 中文 / English switch only when both exist. The site menus stay in Chinese.\n- (c) Same as (b), plus a fully translated English version of the site's menus and labels (a second copy of the site under `en/`).\n- (d) Same as (c), plus automatic AI translation inside the CMS.\n\n➡️ (b). It matches what you said (\"editor can upload either language, or both\") and costs one extra field and a toggle. Translation happens outside the CMS, where the writer can check the game terms. I'd write (c) down as a stretch goal and leave (d) out of scope."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1130,"cache_read_input_tokens":68008,"output_tokens":2502,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":116},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1130,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":2502,"cache_read_input_tokens":68008,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1130,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1130},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011Cg67bwcePvWJb49H96qQ9","type":"assistant","uuid":"8c1b236d-4b36-4d65-84d4-31bc6af29666","timestamp":"2026-10-16T14:59:53.675Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"high","perTurnEffort":"high","session_id":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"d1e69fc1-c6bd-41bf-a746-f18c4278d904","version":"2.1.288","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}

{"parentUuid":"c1316288-9ed3-4178-b0db-60a2c4d54640","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg69Hnr2V4xuGHthmNwD6","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01WPYbPzGXxxk6siJX7Vayxn","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2/CONTEXT.md","content":"# The Bazaar Guide Site (大巴扎攻略站)\n\nA small CMS where streamers (up主) and invited writers in the Chinese-speaking\ncommunity of the card game The Bazaar publish written guides, so players can\nfind a build for a given hero and patch without scrubbing through videos.\n\n## Language\n\n### People\n\n**Admin** (管理员):\nOne of the few top streamers who run the site. Reviews and publishes other\npeople's Guides and manages users.\n_Avoid_: owner, superuser\n\n**Editor** (编辑):\nAn invited guide writer (another up主 or an experienced player). Writes\nGuides but cannot publish them or manage users.\n_Avoid_: author (as a role name), contributor, writer\n\n**Reader** (读者):\nAnyone who plays the game and reads the public site. Has no account.\n_Avoid_: user, visitor, member\n\n### Content\n\n**Guide** (攻略):\nA written strategy piece about one Hero on one Patch, typically built around\nscreenshots of a lineup or deck with an explanation of how it plays. Guides\nfor tournament mode are still Guides.\n_Avoid_: article, tutorial, post\n\n**Page** (页面):\nA standalone piece of site content written by an Admin, such as About (关于),\nthat appears in the public navigation.\n_Avoid_: static page\n\n### The game\n\n**Game Term** (游戏术语):\nA named thing in The Bazaar (a Hero, a card, a skill) that has an official\nChinese name and an official English name, stored as a pair.\n_Avoid_: keyword, tag, entity\n\n**Hero** (英雄):\nThe Game Term for a playable character. Every Guide is about exactly one Hero.\n_Avoid_: character, class\n\n**Official name** (官方名称):\nThe name the game itself uses for a Game Term in a given language. The site\nonly ever shows Official names.\n_Avoid_: nickname (外号), alias, translation\n\n**Patch** (版本):\nThe game version a Guide was written for, such as `6.7`. Picked by the\nwriter. It describes when the Guide was written and is not a verdict on\nwhether the Guide is out of date.\n_Avoid_: version (also used for edits to a Guide), season\n\n**Current Patch** (当前版本):\nThe newest Patch of the game, as set by an Admin.\n_Avoid_: latest version, live patch\n\n**Tournament** (锦标赛):\nAn experimental game mode in which many players (up to about 100) play one\ngame together until there is one champion. It has its own section on the site.\n_Avoid_: event, competition, league\n\n### Workflow\n\n**Draft** (草稿):\nA Guide its writer has not finished yet. Only its writer and Admins can see it.\n_Avoid_: unpublished\n\n**Submitted** (待审核):\nA Guide its writer has marked finished, waiting for an Admin to review it.\n_Avoid_: pending, draft, ready\n\n**Return** (退回):\nAn Admin's decision that a Submitted Guide is not ready. It goes back to its\nwriter as a Draft, with the Admin's notes.\n_Avoid_: reject, decline\n\n**Publish** (发布):\nAn Admin's approval of a Submitted Guide, which makes it Published. Publishing\ndoes not by itself change the public site.\n_Avoid_: approve, go live\n\n**Published** (已发布):\nA Guide an Admin has approved. It will appear on the public site after the\nnext Site build.\n_Avoid_: live, approved\n\n**Revision** (修订):\nA proposed change to a Published Guide. While it waits for review the\nPublished Guide stays on the site unchanged. Once published, it replaces the\nold content and the old content is not shown.\n_Avoid_: version, new version, edit\n\n**Site build** (更新网站):\nRegenerating the public site from everything that is Published, and putting it\nonline. This is the only step that changes what Readers see.\n_Avoid_: publish, deploy, export\n\n## Flagged ambiguities\n\n- \"Draft\" was being used for both an unfinished Guide and a finished one\n  awaiting review. Those are now **Draft** and **Submitted**.\n- \"Version\" can mean the game's Patch or an edit to a Guide. Use **Patch** for\n  the game and **Revision** for an edit.\n- \"Publish\" meant both an Admin's approval and regenerating the site. Approval\n  is **Publish**; regenerating is **Site build**. An Editor never publishes:\n  their button is Submit (提交审核).\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":565,"cache_read_input_tokens":71640,"output_tokens":4689,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":3118},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":565,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":4689,"cache_read_input_tokens":71640,"cache_creation_input_tokens":565,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":565},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01WPYbPzGXxxk6siJX7Vayxn":{"file_path":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2/CONTEXT.md","content":"# The Bazaar Guide Site (大巴扎攻略站)\n\nA small CMS where streamers (up主) and invited writers in the Chinese-speaking\ncommunity of the card game The Bazaar publish written guides, so players can\nfind a build for a given hero and patch without scrubbing through videos.\n\n## Language\n\n### People\n\n**Admin** (管理员):\nOne of the few top streamers who run the site. It describes when the Guide was written and is not a verdict on\nwhether the Guide is out of date.\n_Avoid_: version (also used for edits to a Guide), season\n\n**Page** (页面):\nA standalone piece of site content written by an Admin, such as About (关于),\nthat appears in the public navigation.\n_Avoid_: static page\n\n### Workflow\n\n**Draft** (草稿):\nA Guide its writer has not finished yet. Only its writer and Admins can see it.\n_Avoid_: unpublished\n\n**Submitted** (待审核):\nA Guide its writer has marked finished, waiting for an Admin to review it.\n_Avoid_: pending, draft, ready\n\n**Published** (已发布):\nA Guide an Admin has approved. It is eligible to appear on the public site.\n_Avoid_: live, approved\n\n## Flagged ambiguities\n\n- \"Draft\" was being used for both an unfinished Guide and a finished one\n  awaiting review. Those are now **Draft** and **Submitted**.\n- \"Version\" can mean the game's Patch or an edit to a Guide. Use **Patch** for\n  the game.\n","userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"9ee6935f-3d53-4052-9ec8-bd3123834dba","session_id":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"d1e69fc1-c6bd-41bf-a746-f18c4278d904","version":"2.1.288","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}

{"parentUuid":"a16142bf-1bd1-496a-b9e2-ec8aad8af118","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg69MUFSQjavh5bEtzzzz","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I've updated `CONTEXT.md`. It now has Game Term, Official name, Current Patch, Tournament, Return, Publish, Revision, and Site build. I took out the Mode idea, since tournament guides now go under Guides. Round 3:\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q1** - **What's actually in the Tournaments section now?** Tournament guides moved to Guides, so 锦标赛 is left with an explanation of how tournament mode works, plus recaps (who won and what builds placed). Options:\n\n- (a) Tournaments is a **Page**, like About. An admin keeps one page up to date, with the mode explained at the top and recaps added below.\n- (b) Tournaments is a list of **Recap** posts, each its own item with a date and a Patch. This is a second content type.\n\n➡️ (a). The mode is still being tested and recaps will be rare. Making it a Page means the nav works through capability 4 for free, at no extra cost. If tournaments take off, a Recap content type is a clean later addition.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q2** - **How does the Patch picker look, and does the public site show the Current Patch?** You want the editor to see something like `v6.7（当前）` and at most two older patches. My proposal:\n\n- An admin adds a new Patch, and that automatically makes it the Current Patch.\n- The editor's dropdown shows `6.7（当前版本）`, `6.6`, `6.5`, with the current one preselected. Older patches aren't offered.\n- If an editor revises an old guide that's still on, say, 6.3, its existing patch still shows as the selected value, so nothing is lost.\n- The public site shows \"当前版本 6.7\" in the header and the Patch on every guide, so readers compare for themselves. That fits your choice of (b): no \"outdated\" label.\n\n➡️ As described above. One check: should the public header show the Current Patch? I think it helps readers without judging any guide.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q3** - **How do review notes and the \"not approved\" notification work?** You want the admin to point at the part of the guide that's wrong. True highlighting (selecting text inside the editor) needs JavaScript we don't otherwise have. It also breaks easily: once the editor rewrites that paragraph, the highlight has nothing to attach to. Options:\n\n- (a) One free-text note per Return.\n- (b) A Return carries a list of **Review notes**. Each note has a **quoted passage** (the admin copies a line from the guide) and the admin's advice. The editor sees the notes at the top of their Draft, and quoted lines that are still in the text are highlighted in the preview.\n- (c) Real inline highlighting in the editor.\n\nThere's also the notification. The console is local-only and there's no email, so the \"notification\" would be a badge on the editor's dashboard (\"1 篇攻略被退回\").\n\n➡️ (b) plus the dashboard badge. It gives the editor \"this part, and here's why\" without fragile JavaScript. Notes stay attached to the guide so there's a history if it goes back and forth.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q4** - **The rules for a Revision.** You picked (c): the live guide stays up while the change waits for review. The edge cases:\n\n- A Revision follows the same Draft → Submitted flow, so an editor can save a half-done Revision and come back to it.\n- Each Guide has **at most one open Revision** at a time.\n- If an admin Returns a Revision, the live guide is untouched and the Revision goes back to the editor as a Draft.\n- When an **admin** edits a Published guide, the change takes effect immediately with no review step, because admins are the reviewers.\n- Readers see \"更新于 <date>\" and the guide's current Patch. Old content is not shown (your call).\n- If the Revision changes the Patch (6.7 → 6.8), the guide moves to the 6.8 group on its Hero's page.\n\n➡️ All of the above. The one I most want you to confirm is admin edits going live without review.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q5** - **How many Game Terms, and who enters them?** The Bazaar has dozens of heroes and skills and well over a thousand items/cards, all with official zh/en names. Nobody will type a thousand pairs by hand, and as far as I know the game has no official data export. Options:\n\n- (a) Heroes only. Admins enter them by hand (a small list).\n- (b) Heroes, plus cards and skills that **admins add as they come up**, one at a time in the console.\n- (c) Same as (b), plus **CSV import**, so a list from a fan wiki or a community spreadsheet can be loaded in one go. Admins check what's imported.\n\n➡️ (c). Heroes are needed on day one. Cards and skills grow as guides need them, and CSV import is how you'd fill the list properly. `csv` is part of Python's standard library, so no new dependency. One check: in your answer you wrote \"heros, **games**, and cards\". Did you mean **skills**? Are there other kinds of things that need official names (items vs cards, enchantments, monsters)?\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q6** - **How does an editor mark a Game Term in a guide, and what does marking it do?** One proposal is a Markdown marker such as `[[瓦妮莎]]` or `[[Vanessa]]`. On the public site:\n\n- It renders as the **Official name in that body's language**. `[[瓦妮莎]]` inside the English body becomes \"Vanessa\", so an AI-translated English body still gets every game name right.\n- It's visually styled as a game term.\n- The preview **warns** about any `[[…]]` that matches no Game Term, so editors find typos and nicknames.\n- Optionally, admins record known **nicknames** against a term, and the preview warns \"'瓦姐' 是外号，请使用 [[瓦妮莎]]\" when one appears unmarked.\n\nA warning still allows the guide to be Submitted, since the admin reviewer is the backstop. The alternative is to block Submission, which is stricter but could leave editors stuck on a term nobody has added yet.\n\n➡️ The marker plus warnings, with the nickname list included. It's cheap, and it's the only way plain text ever gets checked for nicknames. Warnings shouldn't block Submission.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q7** - **What do language and the bilingual site mean in practice?** With (c), each Guide has a Chinese body, an English body, or both, and the site's menus and labels exist in both languages (a 中文 / English switch). Remaining choices:\n\n- What does an English reader see for a guide with **only a Chinese body**? Hidden, or listed with a \"中文 only\" badge?\n- Is the **admin console** bilingual too, or Chinese only?\n- What does the site open in by default?\n\n➡️ The guide is listed with a language badge. Screenshots of the build are useful even when you can't read the text, and hiding it would make the English site look empty. The console is Chinese only, since every admin and editor is a Chinese speaker. The site defaults to Chinese, and the switch keeps you on the same page in the other language.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q8** - **How are authors shown, and what happens when someone leaves?** \"Browse by author\" needs a public name.\n\n- Each user has a **display name** (their Bilibili name) shown publicly. Login usernames are never shown on the public site.\n- When an admin **deactivates** an editor, that editor's Published guides stay on the site under their name. Deactivation blocks login, not content. The editor's open Drafts and Revisions stay where they are; admins can still see and delete them.\n- Guides written by admins appear under the admin's display name like anyone else's.\n\n➡️ As described above. Do you want any author-page extras beyond a name and the author's guide list? A one-line bio or a link to their Bilibili space would be cheap."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":4795,"cache_read_input_tokens":72205,"output_tokens":2578,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":32},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":4795,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":2578,"cache_read_input_tokens":72205,"cache_creation_input_tokens":4795,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":4795},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011Cg69MTwqwkVffhGmJ133t","type":"assistant","uuid":"be0bd220-e6eb-432e-961d-cab998028d4e","timestamp":"2026-10-16T15:22:50.499Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"high","perTurnEffort":"high","session_id":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"d1e69fc1-c6bd-41bf-a746-f18c4278d904","version":"2.1.288","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}

Readers can browse all of an Author's\nPublished Guides on that Author's page.\n_Avoid_: owner, creator, up主 (not every Author is a streamer)\n\n**Display name** (昵称):\nThe name an Author chooses to be shown under publicly. It is never their\nlogin username.\n_Avoid_: username, handle","originalFile":"# The Bazaar Guide Site (大巴扎攻略站)\n\nA small CMS where streamers (up主) and invited writers in the Chinese-speaking\ncommunity of the card game The Bazaar publish written guides, so players can\nfind a build for a given hero and patch without scrubbing through videos.\n\n## Language\n\n### People\n\n**Admin** (管理员):\nOne of the few top streamers who run the site. Reviews and publishes other\npeople's Guides and manages users.\n_Avoid_: owner, superuser\n\n**Editor** (编辑):\nAn invited guide writer (another up主 or an experienced player). Writes\nGuides but cannot publish them or manage users.\n_Avoid_: author (as a role name), contributor, writer\n\n**Reader** (读者):\nAnyone who plays the game and reads the public site. Has no account.\n_Avoid_: user, visitor, member\n\n### Content\n\n**Guide** (攻略):\nA written strategy piece about one Hero on one Patch, typically built around\nscreenshots of a lineup or deck with an explanation of how it plays. Guides\nfor tournament mode are still Guides.\n_Avoid_: article, tutorial, post\n\n**Page** (页面):\nA standalone piece of site content written by an Admin, such as About (关于),\nthat appears in the public navigation.\n_Avoid_: static page\n\n### The game\n\n**Game Term** (游戏术语):\nA named thing in The Bazaar (a Hero, a card, a skill) that has an official\nChinese name and an official English name, stored as a pair.\n_Avoid_: keyword, tag, entity\n\n**Hero** (英雄):\nThe Game Term for a playable character. Every Guide is about exactly one Hero.\n_Avoid_: character, class\n\n**Official name** (官方名称):\nThe name the game itself uses for a Game Term in a given language. The site\nonly ever shows Official names.\n_Avoid_: nickname (外号), alias, translation\n\n**Patch** (版本):\nThe game version a Guide was written for, such as `6.7`. Picked by the\nwriter. It describes when the Guide was written and is not a verdict on\nwhether the Guide is out of date.\n_Avoid_: version (also used for edits to a Guide), season\n\n**Current Patch** (当前版本):\nThe newest Patch of the game, as set by an Admin.\n_Avoid_: latest version, live patch\n\n**Tournament** (锦标赛):\nAn experimental game mode in which many players (up to about 100) play one\ngame together until there is one champion. It has its own section on the site.\n_Avoid_: event, competition, league\n\n### Workflow\n\n**Draft** (草稿):\nA Guide its writer has not finished yet. Only its writer and Admins can see it.\n_Avoid_: unpublished\n\n**Submitted** (待审核):\nA Guide its writer has marked finished, waiting for an Admin to review it.\n_Avoid_: pending, draft, ready\n\n**Return** (退回):\nAn Admin's decision that a Submitted Guide is not ready. It goes back to its\nwriter as a Draft, with the Admin's notes.\n_Avoid_: reject, decline\n\n**Publish** (发布):\nAn Admin's approval of a Submitted Guide, which makes it Published. Publishing\ndoes not by itself change the public site.\n_Avoid_: approve, go live\n\n**Published** (已发布):\nA Guide an Admin has approved. It will appear on the public site after the\nnext Site build.\n_Avoid_: live, approved\n\n**Revision** (修订):\nA proposed change to a Published Guide. While it waits for review the\nPublished Guide stays on the site unchanged. Once published, it replaces the\nold content and the old content is not shown.\n_Avoid_: version, new version, edit\n\n**Site build** (更新网站):\nRegenerating the public site from everything that is Published, and putting it\nonline. This is the only step that changes what Readers see.\n_Avoid_: publish, deploy, export\n\n## Flagged ambiguities\n\n- \"Draft\" was being used for both an unfinished Guide and a finished one\n  awaiting review. Those are now **Draft** and **Submitted**.\n- \"Version\" can mean the game's Patch or an edit to a Guide. Use **Patch** for\n  the game and **Revision** for an edit.\n- \"Publish\" meant both an Admin's approval and regenerating the site. Approval\n  is **Publish**; regenerating is **Site build**. An Editor never publishes:\n  their button is Submit (提交审核).\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":22,"oldLines":6,"newStart":22,"newLines":16,"lines":[" Anyone who plays the game and reads the public site. Has no account."," _Avoid_: user, visitor, member"," ","+**Author** (作者):","+The Admin or Editor who wrote a Guide. It is never their","+login username.","+_Avoid_: username, handle","+"," ### Content"," "," **Guide** (攻略):"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"409106b0-7b97-4c2c-bd9d-0eb22f1d027e","session_id":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"d1e69fc1-c6bd-41bf-a746-f18c4278d904","version":"2.1.288","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}

(file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"uuid":"f22d0595-8841-4319-bbaf-6f0d35018ca1","timestamp":"2026-10-17T04:37:53.838Z","toolUseResult":{"filePath":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2/CONTEXT.md","oldString":"_Avoid_: reject, decline\n\n","newString":"_Avoid_: reject, decline\n\n**Review note** (审核意见):\nPart of a Return: a passage quoted from the Guide together with the Admin's\nadvice on how to fix it.\n_Avoid_: comment (comments stay on Bilibili), feedback\n\n","originalFile":"# The Bazaar Guide Site (大巴扎攻略站)\n\nA small CMS where streamers (up主) and invited writers in the Chinese-speaking\ncommunity of the card game The Bazaar publish written guides, so players can\nfind a build for a given hero and patch without scrubbing through videos.\n\n## Language\n\n### People\n\n**Admin** (管理员):\nOne of the few top streamers who run the site. Reviews and publishes other\npeople's Guides and manages users.\n_Avoid_: owner, superuser\n\n**Editor** (编辑):\nAn invited guide writer (another up主 or an experienced player). Writes\nGuides but cannot publish them or manage users.\n_Avoid_: author (as a role name), contributor, writer\n\n**Reader** (读者):\nAnyone who plays the game and reads the public site. Has no account.\n_Avoid_: user, visitor, member\n\n**Author** (作者):\nThe Admin or Editor who wrote a Guide. Readers can browse all of an Author's\nPublished Guides on that Author's page.\n_Avoid_: owner, creator, up主 (not every Author is a streamer)\n\n**Display name** (昵称):\nThe name an Author chooses to be shown under publicly. It is never their\nlogin username.\n_Avoid_: username, handle\n\n### Content\n\n**Guide** (攻略):\nA written strategy piece about one Hero on one Patch, typically built around\nscreenshots of a lineup or deck with an explanation of how it plays. Guides\nfor tournament mode are still Guides.\n_Avoid_: article, tutorial, post\n\n**Page** (页面):\nA standalone piece of site content written by an Admin, such as About (关于),\nthat appears in the public navigation.\n_Avoid_: static page\n\n### The game\n\n**Game Term** (游戏术语):\nA named thing in The Bazaar (a Hero, a card, a skill) that has an official\nChinese name and an official English name, stored as a pair.\n_Avoid_: keyword, tag, entity\n\n**Hero** (英雄):\nThe Game Term for a playable character. Every Guide is about exactly one Hero.\n_Avoid_: character, class\n\n**Official name** (官方名称):\nThe name the game itself uses for a Game Term in a given language. The site\nonly ever shows Official names.\n_Avoid_: nickname (外号), alias, translation\n\n**Patch** (版本):\nThe game version a Guide was written for, such as `6.7`. Picked by the\nwriter. It describes when the Guide was written and is not a verdict on\nwhether the Guide is out of date.\n_Avoid_: version (also used for edits to a Guide), season\n\n**Current Patch** (当前版本):\nThe newest Patch of the game, as set by an Admin.\n_Avoid_: latest version, live patch\n\n**Tournament** (锦标赛):\nAn experimental game mode in which many players (up to about 100) play one\ngame together until there is one champion. It has its own section on the site.\n_Avoid_: event, competition, league\n\n### Workflow\n\n**Draft** (草稿):\nA Guide its writer has not finished yet. Only its writer and Admins can see it.\n_Avoid_: unpublished\n\n**Submitted** (待审核):\nA Guide its writer has marked finished, waiting for an Admin to review it.\n_Avoid_: pending, draft, ready\n\n**Return** (退回):\nAn Admin's decision that a Submitted Guide is not ready. It goes back to its\nwriter as a Draft, with the Admin's notes.\n_Avoid_: reject, decline\n\n**Publish** (发布):\nAn Admin's approval of a Submitted Guide, which makes it Published. Publishing\ndoes not by itself change the public site.\n_Avoid_: approve, go live\n\n**Published** (已发布):\nA Guide an Admin has approved. It will appear on the public site after the\nnext Site build.\n_Avoid_: live, approved\n\n**Revision** (修订):\nA proposed change to a Published Guide. While it waits for review the\nPublished Guide stays on the site unchanged. Once published, it replaces the\nold content and the old content is not shown.\n_Avoid_: version, new version, edit\n\n**Site build** (更新网站):\nRegenerating the public site from everything that is Published, and putting it\nonline. This is the only step that changes what Readers see.\n_Avoid_: publish, deploy, export\n\n## Flagged ambiguities\n\n- \"Draft\" was being used for both an unfinished Guide and a finished one\n  awaiting review. Those are now **Draft** and **Submitted**.\n- \"Version\" can mean the game's Patch or an edit to a Guide. Use **Patch** for\n  the game and **Revision** for an edit.\n- \"Publish\" meant both an Admin's approval and regenerating the site. Approval\n  is **Publish**; regenerating is **Site build**. An Editor never publishes:\n  their button is Submit (提交审核).\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":91,"oldLines":6,"newStart":91,"newLines":11,"lines":[" writer as a Draft, with the Admin's notes."," _Avoid_: reject, decline"," ","+**Review note** (审核意见):","+Part of a Return: a passage quoted from the Guide together with the Admin's","+advice on how to fix it.","+_Avoid_: comment (comments stay on Bilibili), feedback","+"," **Publish** (发布):"," An Admin's approval of a Submitted Guide, which makes it Published. Reviews and publishes other\npeople's Guides and manages users.\n_Avoid_: owner, superuser\n\n**Editor** (编辑):\nAn invited guide writer (another up主 or an experienced player). Writes\nGuides but cannot publish them or manage users.\n_Avoid_: author (as a role name), contributor, writer\n\n**Reader** (读者):\nAnyone who plays the game and reads the public site. Readers can browse all of an Author's\nPublished Guides on that Author's page.\n_Avoid_: owner, creator, up主 (not every Author is a streamer)\n\n**Display name** (昵称):\nThe name an Author chooses to be shown under publicly. It is never their\nlogin username.\n_Avoid_: username, handle\n\n### Content\n\n**Guide** (攻略):\nA written strategy piece about one Hero on one Patch, typically built around\nscreenshots of a lineup or deck with an explanation of how it plays. Every Guide is about exactly one Hero.\n_Avoid_: character, class\n\n**Official name** (官方名称):\nThe name the game itself uses for a Game Term in a given language. The site\nonly ever shows Official names.\n_Avoid_: nickname (外号), alias, translation\n\n**Patch** (版本):\nThe game version a Guide was written for, such as `6.7`. Picked by the\nwriter. It describes when the Guide was written and is not a verdict on\nwhether the Guide is out of date.\n_Avoid_: version (also used for edits to a Guide), season\n\n**Current Patch** (当前版本):\nThe newest Patch of the game, as set by an Admin.\n_Avoid_: latest version, live patch\n\n**Tournament** (锦标赛):\nAn experimental game mode in which many players (up to about 100) play one\ngame together until there is one champion. It has its own section on the site.\n_Avoid_: event, competition, league\n\n### Workflow\n\n**Draft** (草稿):\nA Guide its writer has not finished yet. Only its writer and Admins can see it.\n_Avoid_: unpublished\n\n**Submitted** (待审核):\nA Guide its writer has marked finished, waiting for an Admin to review it.\n_Avoid_: pending, draft, ready\n\n**Return** (退回):\nAn Admin's decision that a Submitted Guide is not ready. It goes back to its\nwriter as a Draft, with the Admin's notes.\n_Avoid_: reject, decline\n\n**Review note** (审核意见):\nPart of a Return: a passage quoted from the Guide together with the Admin's\nadvice on how to fix it.\n_Avoid_: comment (comments stay on Bilibili), feedback\n\n**Publish** (发布):\nAn Admin's approval of a Submitted Guide, which makes it Published. Publishing\ndoes not by itself change the public site.\n_Avoid_: approve, go live\n\n**Published** (已发布):\nA Guide an Admin has approved. It will appear on the public site after the\nnext Site build.\n_Avoid_: live, approved\n\n**Revision** (修订):\nA proposed change to a Published Guide. While it waits for review the\nPublished Guide stays on the site unchanged. Once published, it replaces the\nold content and the old content is not shown.\n_Avoid_: version, new version, edit\n\n**Site build** (更新网站):\nRegenerating the public site from everything that is Published, and putting it\nonline. This is the only step that changes what Readers see.\n_Avoid_: publish, deploy, export\n\n## Flagged ambiguities\n\n- \"Draft\" was being used for both an unfinished Guide and a finished one\n  awaiting review.
