{"parentUuid":"55114f8d-4dbe-4e0d-bb01-d18b7c17305a","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg7C1zk3Texr1JeRCFdW7","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I've added Author, Display name and Review note to `CONTEXT.md`, and widened Game Term to cover items, skills, enchantments and monsters. Two of your answers raised new questions (Q1 and Q3). Round 4:\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q1** - **Is Tournaments one Page, or a list of entries?** You said it holds recaps of past tournaments and information about upcoming ones. That sounds like a stream of items over time. There are three ways to model it:\n\n- (a) **One Page** an admin keeps editing: upcoming events at the top, recaps further down. This is the cheapest option and is covered by capability 4.\n- (b) A list of **Tournament announcements (赛事公告)**: one item per tournament, each with a date and Patch. The item is written before the event as \"upcoming\" and *updated into* its recap afterwards. The Tournaments menu lists them newest first, and only admins write them.\n- (c) Same as (b), but the announcement and the recap are two separate items.\n\nRelated: is a \"tournament\" here something the game itself runs on a schedule, or something streamers or the community organize?\n\n➡️ (b). One entry per event, updated from announcement to recap, matches how a tournament actually unfolds, and it gives readers a dated history. Admins write them, using the same Draft/Published flow but without review, since admins publish directly. If tournaments stay rare, (a) is a fine fallback.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q2** - **Are \"card\" and \"item\" the same thing?** In the game's English these are *Items*. Players (and you, earlier) often say *cards*. The glossary needs one word. I also want to confirm the full list of Game Term kinds: **Hero, Item, Skill, Enchantment, Monster**. Is anything missing, such as merchants or events?\n\n➡️ Use **Item** (物品), with \"card\" under _Avoid_, and the kinds as listed. If the community's Chinese word is 卡牌 rather than 物品, tell me and I'll use the official in-game Chinese word.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q3** - **What happens to a guide that exists in only one language?** You want the switch to put the *whole* site, guides included, into one language. Since we aren't translating inside the CMS, a Chinese-only guide has no English text to show. Options:\n\n- (a) **Every Published guide must have both languages.** Editors bring their own translation (AI outside the CMS is fine), and admins won't publish a guide that has only one. The two sites always match, but every writer has a heavier job.\n- (b) **Each guide appears only in the languages it has.** A Chinese-only guide is listed on the Chinese site and doesn't appear on the English site. If a reader switches language while on that guide, they land on the same Hero's page in the other language with a short notice (\"This guide is only available in Chinese\").\n- (c) Chinese required, English optional, with (b)'s behavior.\n\nIn all cases the title is per language too, and `[[Game Term]]` markers render in the reader's language automatically.\n\n➡️ (b). It keeps your \"either or both\" rule and never mixes languages on a page. The English site will start thinner, which is honest. An English-speaking writer can still write English-only.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q4** - **What do guide URLs look like?** Capability 3 requires a slug. Chinese titles can't be turned into clean URL slugs without a pinyin library (a new dependency), and titles change when a guide is revised. Options:\n\n- (a) The editor types an ASCII slug for every guide.\n- (b) The slug is auto-built from the **Hero's English official name plus a number**, e.g. `guides/vanessa-12/`. Admins can edit it. It never changes when the title changes.\n- (c) Auto-built from the English title when there is one, otherwise (b).\n\nHero pages get their slugs the same way (`heroes/vanessa/`), which is free now that every Hero has an English official name.\n\n➡️ (b). Editors never have to think about it (they're not tech-comfortable), links shared on Bilibili never break after a Revision, and it works the same for Chinese-only guides.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q5** - **How are Display names and author pages handled?** Capability 6 says *admins* create accounts, so \"they decide their own name when creating accounts\" needs a mechanism:\n\n- The admin creates the account with a username and a temporary password. On first login, the editor sets their own **Display name**, and can change it later in their profile.\n- Display names must be unique. Two authors shown as \"老王\" would merge in readers' minds.\n- Every Author with at least one Published guide gets an author page. Its URL uses a number or an admin-set ASCII slug (`authors/7/`), never the login username, because exposing usernames on a public site helps anyone guessing at logins.\n\n➡️ As described above. Do authors with no Published guides yet get an author page? I'd say no; an empty author page looks broken.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q6** - **The full permission split.** Your brief says editors \"only write guides\". Spelled out:\n\n| | Editor | Admin |\n|---|---|---|\n| Create guides, save Drafts, Submit | own | any |\n| See other people's Drafts/Submitted guides | ✗ | ✓ |\n| Publish, Return, edit Published guides directly | ✗ | ✓ |\n| Open a Revision on a Published guide | own | — (edits go live directly) |\n| Delete a guide | own Drafts only | any |\n| Pages, Tournament entries, Game Terms, Patches | ✗ | ✓ |\n| Upload images | ✓ (into their own guides) | ✓ |\n| Users: create, change role, deactivate | ✗ | ✓ |\n| Run the Site build | ✗ | ✓ |\n\nThere are also two guards against locking yourself out: an admin can't deactivate or demote themselves, and the last active admin can never be removed.\n\n➡️ The table as shown. The cell to check is **editors can't delete their own Published guides**. Removing a live guide is an admin decision, and the editor asks an admin.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q7** - **What does the admin dashboard show?** Capability 5 requires counts, a filterable content list, and an editor with a preview. For streamers who aren't comfortable with computers, I'd put these counts at the top:\n\n- **For admins:** 待审核 (Submitted guides and Revisions), guides Published but not yet on the site (\"N 项更改尚未更新到网站\", with the Site build button next to it), and totals by status.\n- **For editors:** my Drafts, my Submitted guides, and **my Returned guides** (the badge from Q3 last round).\n- **Content list filters:** status, Hero, Author, Patch, language.\n- **Editor preview:** shows the guide as Readers will see it, with `[[term]]` and nickname warnings.\n\n➡️ As described above. Is there anything a streamer would look for first that's missing?\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q8** - **What do Readers see first?** I'd suggest the public home page shows the Current Patch, the newest Published guides, and a grid of Heroes. List items show title, Hero, Patch, Author and date. Should a guide also have a **cover image**, the lineup screenshot that shows on list pages? Guides are built around screenshots, so a visual list would beat a wall of Chinese titles.\n\n➡️ Yes. The cover is chosen from the guide's own uploaded images, defaulting to the first one. The home page layout is as listed above.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q9** - **What's explicitly out of scope?** The list I'd write into the spec:\n\n- Comments and discussion (stay on Bilibili)\n- Reader accounts\n- Search (a static site has no server; Hero, Author and Patch browsing covers the need)\n- Translation inside the CMS (AI or machine)\n- A card database or patch-notes section (the wiki already covers it)\n- Scheduled publishing\n- The manual's exclusions: multi-site, drag-and-drop builders, WYSIWYG editors\n\n➡️ All of the above. Is anything on this list something you'd fight for?"}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":3795,"cache_read_input_tokens":79909,"output_tokens":2679,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":32},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":3795,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":2679,"cache_read_input_tokens":79909,"cache_creation_input_tokens":3795,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":3795},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011Cg7C1zURpKE9M7YwZaWse","type":"assistant","uuid":"0f281634-c821-492a-9102-b7d1e7809cd2","timestamp":"2026-10-17T04:38:23.021Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"high","perTurnEffort":"high","session_id":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"d1e69fc1-c6bd-41bf-a746-f18c4278d904","version":"2.1.288","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}

It is a\nseparate item from that Tournament's announcement.\n_Avoid_: event, report, result\n\n**Chinese text / English text** (中文版 / 英文版):\nThe two language versions of a Guide (or other content), each with its own\ntitle and body. Chinese is required. English is optional, and content without\nit does not appear on the English site.\n_Avoid_: translation, localization, body","originalFile":"# The Bazaar Guide Site (大巴扎攻略站)\n\nA small CMS where streamers (up主) and invited writers in the Chinese-speaking\ncommunity of the card game The Bazaar publish written guides, so players can\nfind a build for a given hero and patch without scrubbing through videos.\n\n## Language\n\n### People\n\n**Admin** (管理员):\nOne of the few top streamers who run the site. Reviews and publishes other\npeople's Guides and manages users.\n_Avoid_: owner, superuser\n\n**Editor** (编辑):\nAn invited guide writer (another up主 or an experienced player). Writes\nGuides but cannot publish them or manage users.\n_Avoid_: author (as a role name), contributor, writer\n\n**Reader** (读者):\nAnyone who plays the game and reads the public site. Has no account.\n_Avoid_: user, visitor, member\n\n**Author** (作者):\nThe Admin or Editor who wrote a Guide. Readers can browse all of an Author's\nPublished Guides on that Author's page.\n_Avoid_: owner, creator, up主 (not every Author is a streamer)\n\n**Display name** (昵称):\nThe name an Author chooses to be shown under publicly. It is never their\nlogin username.\n_Avoid_: username, handle\n\n### Content\n\n**Guide** (攻略):\nA written strategy piece about one Hero on one Patch, typically built around\nscreenshots of a lineup or deck with an explanation of how it plays. Guides\nfor tournament mode are still Guides.\n_Avoid_: article, tutorial, post\n\n**Page** (页面):\nA standalone piece of site content written by an Admin, such as About (关于),\nthat appears in the public navigation.\n_Avoid_: static page\n\n### The game\n\n**Game Term** (游戏术语):\nA named thing in The Bazaar (a Hero, item, skill, enchantment or monster) that has an official\nChinese name and an official English name, stored as a pair.\n_Avoid_: keyword, tag, entity\n\n**Hero** (英雄):\nThe Game Term for a playable character. Every Guide is about exactly one Hero.\n_Avoid_: character, class\n\n**Official name** (官方名称):\nThe name the game itself uses for a Game Term in a given language. The site\nonly ever shows Official names.\n_Avoid_: nickname (外号), alias, translation\n\n**Patch** (版本):\nThe game version a Guide was written for, such as `6.7`. Picked by the\nwriter. It describes when the Guide was written and is not a verdict on\nwhether the Guide is out of date.\n_Avoid_: version (also used for edits to a Guide), season\n\n**Current Patch** (当前版本):\nThe newest Patch of the game, as set by an Admin.\n_Avoid_: latest version, live patch\n\n**Tournament** (锦标赛):\nAn experimental game mode in which many players (up to about 100) play one\ngame together until there is one champion. It has its own section on the site.\n_Avoid_: event, competition, league\n\n### Workflow\n\n**Draft** (草稿):\nA Guide its writer has not finished yet. Only its writer and Admins can see it.\n_Avoid_: unpublished\n\n**Submitted** (待审核):\nA Guide its writer has marked finished, waiting for an Admin to review it.\n_Avoid_: pending, draft, ready\n\n**Return** (退回):\nAn Admin's decision that a Submitted Guide is not ready. It goes back to its\nwriter as a Draft, with the Admin's notes.\n_Avoid_: reject, decline\n\n**Review note** (审核意见):\nPart of a Return: a passage quoted from the Guide together with the Admin's\nadvice on how to fix it.\n_Avoid_: comment (comments stay on Bilibili), feedback\n\n**Publish** (发布):\nAn Admin's approval of a Submitted Guide, which makes it Published. Publishing\ndoes not by itself change the public site.\n_Avoid_: approve, go live\n\n**Published** (已发布):\nA Guide an Admin has approved. It will appear on the public site after the\nnext Site build.\n_Avoid_: live, approved\n\n**Revision** (修订):\nA proposed change to a Published Guide. While it waits for review the\nPublished Guide stays on the site unchanged. Once published, it replaces the\nold content and the old content is not shown.\n_Avoid_: version, new version, edit\n\n**Site build** (更新网站):\nRegenerating the public site from everything that is Published, and putting it\nonline. This is the only step that changes what Readers see.\n_Avoid_: publish, deploy, export\n\n## Flagged ambiguities\n\n- \"Draft\" was being used for both an unfinished Guide and a finished one\n  awaiting review. Those are now **Draft** and **Submitted**.\n- \"Version\" can mean the game's Patch or an edit to a Guide. Use **Patch** for\n  the game and **Revision** for an edit.\n- \"Publish\" meant both an Admin's approval and regenerating the site. Approval\n  is **Publish**; regenerating is **Site build**. An Editor never publishes:\n  their button is Submit (提交审核).\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":45,"oldLines":6,"newStart":45,"newLines":21,"lines":[" that appears in the public navigation."," _Avoid_: static page"," ","+**Tournament announcement** (锦标赛预告):","+An Admin-written notice about an upcoming in-game Tournament.","+_Avoid_: event, news, post","+","+**Tournament recap** (锦标赛回顾):","+An Admin-written account of a Tournament that has already happened. It is a","+separate item from that Tournament's announcement.","+_Avoid_: event, report, result","+","+**Chinese text / English text** (中文版 / 英文版):","+The two language versions of a Guide (or other content), each with its own","+title and body. Chinese is required. English is optional, and content without","+it does not appear on the English site.","+_Avoid_: translation, localization, body","+"," ### The game"," "," **Game Term** (游戏术语):"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"21503f0b-5008-4ca6-9669-b1de6a1fffd0","session_id":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"d1e69fc1-c6bd-41bf-a746-f18c4278d904","version":"2.1.288","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}

It is one of seven kinds: Hero, Item, Skill,\nEnchantment, Monster, Merchant, or Event.\n_Avoid_: keyword, tag, entity\n\n**Item** (物品):\nThe Game Term kind for the cards a player builds with.\n_Avoid_: card\n\n**Event** (事件):\nThe Game Term kind for an in-game event a player encounters during a run. The\nword means only this; it is never used for a Tournament.\n_Avoid_: using \"event\" for Tournaments or site activity","originalFile":"# The Bazaar Guide Site (大巴扎攻略站)\n\nA small CMS where streamers (up主) and invited writers in the Chinese-speaking\ncommunity of the card game The Bazaar publish written guides, so players can\nfind a build for a given hero and patch without scrubbing through videos.\n\n## Language\n\n### People\n\n**Admin** (管理员):\nOne of the few top streamers who run the site. Reviews and publishes other\npeople's Guides and manages users.\n_Avoid_: owner, superuser\n\n**Editor** (编辑):\nAn invited guide writer (another up主 or an experienced player). Writes\nGuides but cannot publish them or manage users.\n_Avoid_: author (as a role name), contributor, writer\n\n**Reader** (读者):\nAnyone who plays the game and reads the public site. Has no account.\n_Avoid_: user, visitor, member\n\n**Author** (作者):\nThe Admin or Editor who wrote a Guide. Readers can browse all of an Author's\nPublished Guides on that Author's page.\n_Avoid_: owner, creator, up主 (not every Author is a streamer)\n\n**Display name** (昵称):\nThe name an Author chooses to be shown under publicly. It is never their\nlogin username.\n_Avoid_: username, handle\n\n### Content\n\n**Guide** (攻略):\nA written strategy piece about one Hero on one Patch, typically built around\nscreenshots of a lineup or deck with an explanation of how it plays. Guides\nfor tournament mode are still Guides.\n_Avoid_: article, tutorial, post\n\n**Page** (页面):\nA standalone piece of site content written by an Admin, such as About (关于),\nthat appears in the public navigation.\n_Avoid_: static page\n\n**Tournament announcement** (锦标赛预告):\nAn Admin-written notice about an upcoming in-game Tournament.\n_Avoid_: event, news, post\n\n**Tournament recap** (锦标赛回顾):\nAn Admin-written account of a Tournament that has already happened. It is a\nseparate item from that Tournament's announcement.\n_Avoid_: event, report, result\n\n**Chinese text / English text** (中文版 / 英文版):\nThe two language versions of a Guide (or other content), each with its own\ntitle and body. Chinese is required. English is optional, and content without\nit does not appear on the English site.\n_Avoid_: translation, localization, body\n\n### The game\n\n**Game Term** (游戏术语):\nA named thing in The Bazaar (a Hero, item, skill, enchantment or monster) that has an official\nChinese name and an official English name, stored as a pair.\n_Avoid_: keyword, tag, entity\n\n**Hero** (英雄):\nThe Game Term for a playable character. Every Guide is about exactly one Hero.\n_Avoid_: character, class\n\n**Official name** (官方名称):\nThe name the game itself uses for a Game Term in a given language. The site\nonly ever shows Official names.\n_Avoid_: nickname (外号), alias, translation\n\n**Patch** (版本):\nThe game version a Guide was written for, such as `6.7`. Picked by the\nwriter. It describes when the Guide was written and is not a verdict on\nwhether the Guide is out of date.\n_Avoid_: version (also used for edits to a Guide), season\n\n**Current Patch** (当前版本):\nThe newest Patch of the game, as set by an Admin.\n_Avoid_: latest version, live patch\n\n**Tournament** (锦标赛):\nAn experimental game mode in which many players (up to about 100) play one\ngame together until there is one champion. It has its own section on the site.\n_Avoid_: event, competition, league\n\n### Workflow\n\n**Draft** (草稿):\nA Guide its writer has not finished yet. Only its writer and Admins can see it.\n_Avoid_: unpublished\n\n**Submitted** (待审核):\nA Guide its writer has marked finished, waiting for an Admin to review it.\n_Avoid_: pending, draft, ready\n\n**Return** (退回):\nAn Admin's decision that a Submitted Guide is not ready. It goes back to its\nwriter as a Draft, with the Admin's notes.\n_Avoid_: reject, decline\n\n**Review note** (审核意见):\nPart of a Return: a passage quoted from the Guide together with the Admin's\nadvice on how to fix it.\n_Avoid_: comment (comments stay on Bilibili), feedback\n\n**Publish** (发布):\nAn Admin's approval of a Submitted Guide, which makes it Published. Publishing\ndoes not by itself change the public site.\n_Avoid_: approve, go live\n\n**Published** (已发布):\nA Guide an Admin has approved. It will appear on the public site after the\nnext Site build.\n_Avoid_: live, approved\n\n**Revision** (修订):\nA proposed change to a Published Guide. While it waits for review the\nPublished Guide stays on the site unchanged. Once published, it replaces the\nold content and the old content is not shown.\n_Avoid_: version, new version, edit\n\n**Site build** (更新网站):\nRegenerating the public site from everything that is Published, and putting it\nonline. This is the only step that changes what Readers see.\n_Avoid_: publish, deploy, export\n\n## Flagged ambiguities\n\n- \"Draft\" was being used for both an unfinished Guide and a finished one\n  awaiting review. Those are now **Draft** and **Submitted**.\n- \"Version\" can mean the game's Patch or an edit to a Guide. Use **Patch** for\n  the game and **Revision** for an edit.\n- \"Publish\" meant both an Admin's approval and regenerating the site. Approval\n  is **Publish**; regenerating is **Site build**. An Editor never publishes:\n  their button is Submit (提交审核).\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":63,"oldLines":10,"newStart":63,"newLines":20,"lines":[" ### The game"," "," **Game Term** (游戏术语):","-A named thing in The Bazaar (a Hero, item, skill, enchantment or monster) that has an official","-Chinese name and an official English name, stored as a pair.","+A named thing in The Bazaar that has an official Chinese name and an official","+English name, stored as a pair. It is one of seven kinds: Hero, Item, Skill,","+Enchantment, Monster, Merchant, or Event."," _Avoid_: keyword, tag, entity"," ","+**Item** (物品):","+The Game Term kind for the cards a player builds with.","+_Avoid_: card","+","+**Event** (事件):","+The Game Term kind for an in-game event a player encounters during a run. The","+word means only this; it is never used for a Tournament.","+_Avoid_: using \"event\" for Tournaments or site activity","+"," **Hero** (英雄):"," The Game Term for a playable character. Every Guide is about exactly one Hero."," _Avoid_: character, class"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"34afaa7d-8cf8-48ee-b680-3ce7e4c7ef6f","session_id":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"d1e69fc1-c6bd-41bf-a746-f18c4278d904","version":"2.1.288","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}

It has its own section on the site.\n_Avoid_: event, competition, league, match","originalFile":"# The Bazaar Guide Site (大巴扎攻略站)\n\nA small CMS where streamers (up主) and invited writers in the Chinese-speaking\ncommunity of the card game The Bazaar publish written guides, so players can\nfind a build for a given hero and patch without scrubbing through videos.\n\n## Language\n\n### People\n\n**Admin** (管理员):\nOne of the few top streamers who run the site. Reviews and publishes other\npeople's Guides and manages users.\n_Avoid_: owner, superuser\n\n**Editor** (编辑):\nAn invited guide writer (another up主 or an experienced player). Writes\nGuides but cannot publish them or manage users.\n_Avoid_: author (as a role name), contributor, writer\n\n**Reader** (读者):\nAnyone who plays the game and reads the public site. Has no account.\n_Avoid_: user, visitor, member\n\n**Author** (作者):\nThe Admin or Editor who wrote a Guide. Readers can browse all of an Author's\nPublished Guides on that Author's page.\n_Avoid_: owner, creator, up主 (not every Author is a streamer)\n\n**Display name** (昵称):\nThe name an Author chooses to be shown under publicly. It is never their\nlogin username.\n_Avoid_: username, handle\n\n### Content\n\n**Guide** (攻略):\nA written strategy piece about one Hero on one Patch, typically built around\nscreenshots of a lineup or deck with an explanation of how it plays. Guides\nfor tournament mode are still Guides.\n_Avoid_: article, tutorial, post\n\n**Page** (页面):\nA standalone piece of site content written by an Admin, such as About (关于),\nthat appears in the public navigation.\n_Avoid_: static page\n\n**Tournament announcement** (锦标赛预告):\nAn Admin-written notice about an upcoming in-game Tournament.\n_Avoid_: event, news, post\n\n**Tournament recap** (锦标赛回顾):\nAn Admin-written account of a Tournament that has already happened. It is a\nseparate item from that Tournament's announcement.\n_Avoid_: event, report, result\n\n**Chinese text / English text** (中文版 / 英文版):\nThe two language versions of a Guide (or other content), each with its own\ntitle and body. Chinese is required. English is optional, and content without\nit does not appear on the English site.\n_Avoid_: translation, localization, body\n\n### The game\n\n**Game Term** (游戏术语):\nA named thing in The Bazaar that has an official Chinese name and an official\nEnglish name, stored as a pair. It is one of seven kinds: Hero, Item, Skill,\nEnchantment, Monster, Merchant, or Event.\n_Avoid_: keyword, tag, entity\n\n**Item** (物品):\nThe Game Term kind for the cards a player builds with.\n_Avoid_: card\n\n**Event** (事件):\nThe Game Term kind for an in-game event a player encounters during a run. The\nword means only this; it is never used for a Tournament.\n_Avoid_: using \"event\" for Tournaments or site activity\n\n**Hero** (英雄):\nThe Game Term for a playable character. Every Guide is about exactly one Hero.\n_Avoid_: character, class\n\n**Official name** (官方名称):\nThe name the game itself uses for a Game Term in a given language. The site\nonly ever shows Official names.\n_Avoid_: nickname (外号), alias, translation\n\n**Patch** (版本):\nThe game version a Guide was written for, such as `6.7`. Picked by the\nwriter. It describes when the Guide was written and is not a verdict on\nwhether the Guide is out of date.\n_Avoid_: version (also used for edits to a Guide), season\n\n**Current Patch** (当前版本):\nThe newest Patch of the game, as set by an Admin.\n_Avoid_: latest version, live patch\n\n**Tournament** (锦标赛):\nAn experimental game mode in which many players (up to about 100) play one\ngame together until there is one champion. It has its own section on the site.\n_Avoid_: event, competition, league\n\n### Workflow\n\n**Draft** (草稿):\nA Guide its writer has not finished yet. Only its writer and Admins can see it.\n_Avoid_: unpublished\n\n**Submitted** (待审核):\nA Guide its writer has marked finished, waiting for an Admin to review it.\n_Avoid_: pending, draft, ready\n\n**Return** (退回):\nAn Admin's decision that a Submitted Guide is not ready. It goes back to its\nwriter as a Draft, with the Admin's notes.\n_Avoid_: reject, decline\n\n**Review note** (审核意见):\nPart of a Return: a passage quoted from the Guide together with the Admin's\nadvice on how to fix it.\n_Avoid_: comment (comments stay on Bilibili), feedback\n\n**Publish** (发布):\nAn Admin's approval of a Submitted Guide, which makes it Published. Publishing\ndoes not by itself change the public site.\n_Avoid_: approve, go live\n\n**Published** (已发布):\nA Guide an Admin has approved. It will appear on the public site after the\nnext Site build.\n_Avoid_: live, approved\n\n**Revision** (修订):\nA proposed change to a Published Guide. While it waits for review the\nPublished Guide stays on the site unchanged. Once published, it replaces the\nold content and the old content is not shown.\n_Avoid_: version, new version, edit\n\n**Site build** (更新网站):\nRegenerating the public site from everything that is Published, and putting it\nonline. This is the only step that changes what Readers see.\n_Avoid_: publish, deploy, export\n\n## Flagged ambiguities\n\n- \"Draft\" was being used for both an unfinished Guide and a finished one\n  awaiting review. Those are now **Draft** and **Submitted**.\n- \"Version\" can mean the game's Patch or an edit to a Guide. Use **Patch** for\n  the game and **Revision** for an edit.\n- \"Publish\" meant both an Admin's approval and regenerating the site. Approval\n  is **Publish**; regenerating is **Site build**. An Editor never publishes:\n  their button is Submit (提交审核).\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":97,"oldLines":9,"newStart":97,"newLines":10,"lines":[" _Avoid_: latest version, live patch"," "," **Tournament** (锦标赛):","-An experimental game mode in which many players (up to about 100) play one","-game together until there is one champion. It has its own section on the site.","-_Avoid_: event, competition, league","+An experimental in-game mode in which many players (up to about 100) play one","+game together until there is one champion. It is run by the game, not","+organized by players. It has its own section on the site.","+_Avoid_: event, competition, league, match"," "," ### Workflow"," "]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"62b4bd26-3d33-4240-8bea-837a676a9ba4","session_id":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"d1e69fc1-c6bd-41bf-a746-f18c4278d904","version":"2.1.288","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}

{"parentUuid":"c67e1fed-837d-4703-935a-c28ce1018451","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg7ChPe3TkDV2tzksUpbv","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I've updated `CONTEXT.md` with Tournament announcement and Tournament recap as separate items, Chinese text and English text (Chinese required), and the seven Game Term kinds. Item replaces \"card\". I also flagged that **Event** is now a Game Term kind, so it should never mean a tournament. I've noted your Q6 change: editors can delete their own Published guides. Round 5:\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q1** - **How are Tournament announcements and recaps laid out?** Fields I'd give both: Chinese/English text, the Tournament's date, the Patch, and an optional cover image. A recap can link to the announcement it follows.\n\nOne catch comes from the static site: \"upcoming\" depends on today's date, but the site only changes at a Site build. If the Tournaments page splits into \"即将开始\" and \"往期回顾\" by date, an announcement for a tournament that ended yesterday stays under \"upcoming\" until someone runs a build.\n\n- (a) **One list, newest first**, each item badged 预告 or 回顾. Nothing depends on the date at build time.\n- (b) **Two lists split by date** at build time. This reads better, but can be stale between builds.\n\n➡️ (a). It's never wrong, and the badge and date tell readers everything. Admins post the recap soon after anyway.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q2** - **What does \"stop an editor from publishing\" mean?** Editors already can't publish, so I read this as a new account state between active and deactivated: **Submission ban (禁止投稿)**. Proposal:\n\n- A banned editor can still log in, see their guides, and edit their Drafts. They **can't Submit** or open Revisions, and the console shows them why.\n- Their already Published guides **stay on the site**. If an admin wants a specific guide gone, they take it down separately (Q3).\n- They can still delete their own guides, since it's their work.\n- The **Users page** (admin only) lists every account with display name, role, state (active / banned / deactivated), guide counts, and last login. Actions on each row: change role, ban/unban, deactivate/reactivate, reset password.\n\n➡️ As described above. One check: should a ban also **hide all their Published guides** at once? For a \"this person posted something harmful\" situation, that may be what you actually want.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q3** - **Can admins take down a Published guide without deleting it?** Example: a guide turns out to be misleading, or the author asks to rework it heavily.\n\n➡️ Yes: **Unpublish (撤下)**. The guide goes back to its author as a Draft, with an optional Review note explaining why, and it disappears at the next Site build. Nothing is lost, and the author can fix it and Submit again.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q4** - **How does deletion work?** Editors can delete their own Published guides with no review, so a misclick by a streamer who isn't comfortable with computers deletes real work for good. Links already shared in Bilibili comments will break either way.\n\n- (a) Hard delete after a confirmation dialog.\n- (b) Deleted guides go to a **回收站 (trash)** that only admins see. Admins can restore them or empty the trash. The guide is off the site at the next build either way.\n\n➡️ (b). It's a small addition: one state plus an admin list. It turns \"an editor deleted their best guide by accident\" from a disaster into a two-click fix.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q5** - **Where does the console actually run?** This is the biggest gap between your client and the architecture. ADR-001 says the admin console runs **locally on one machine** and never goes on the internet. Your admins and editors are streamers spread around China, each on their own computer. With a local-only console, an editor in Chengdu can't log in to a console running on a streamer's laptop in Shanghai.\n\n- (a) **Accept it for this project.** The console runs on one machine (in practice, the lead streamer's). Login, roles, review, CSRF and the rest are built exactly as if it were shared, and the spec states plainly that real multi-author use needs the console hosted somewhere reachable (the manual's security-gated stretch goal). The demo and grading work as the assignment intends.\n- (b) **Aim for the stretch goal**: a live hosted admin behind a security gate, in scope now.\n- (c) Editors write Markdown offline and send it to an admin, who enters it. This defeats the whole roles and review design.\n\nThere's also a related question: is the **Site build** run from a button in the console (admins only), or only from the `cms publish` command? Your admins won't open a terminal.\n\n➡️ (a), plus a **更新网站 button** in the console that runs the same thing as `cms publish`. This doesn't contradict ADR-001. It's that ADR's stated consequence, and I'll write the multi-machine limitation into the spec as a known gap rather than leave it implied.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q6** - **Does the language rule apply to everything?** You picked \"Chinese required, English optional\" for Guides. Proposal:\n\n- The same rule applies to **Pages, Tournament announcements and recaps**: Chinese required, English optional, and an item without English text doesn't appear on the English site.\n- **Game Terms need both** Official names, since that's the point of the pairs. A CSV row missing one is rejected on import.\n- **Every Hero and Author page exists in both languages**, even if empty in English (\"暂无英文攻略 / No English guides yet\"), so the language switch always has somewhere to land.\n\n➡️ As described above.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q7** - **What are the image limits?** Proposal: PNG, JPG, WebP or GIF only. At most **5 MB** per image, which is enough for a 1080p lineup screenshot. Images belong to a guide and can be used in both its Chinese and English text. Deleting a guide deletes its images. Uploads get a server-generated filename, so nobody can upload `../../something`.\n\n➡️ As described above. If streamers routinely export 4K PowerPoint slides, tell me and I'll raise the limit."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":3290,"cache_read_input_tokens":86642,"output_tokens":3302,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":1334},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":3290,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":3302,"cache_read_input_tokens":86642,"cache_creation_input_tokens":3290,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":3290},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011Cg7ChPNRQpDcJYh7YEBru","type":"assistant","uuid":"5d0cbc01-c249-4239-ba85-cb02283b40d1","timestamp":"2026-10-17T04:47:25.858Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"high","perTurnEffort":"high","session_id":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"d1e69fc1-c6bd-41bf-a746-f18c4278d904","version":"2.1.288","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}

The Guide\ngoes back to its Author as a Draft, optionally with Review notes.\n_Avoid_: hide, archive, take offline\n\n**Published** (已发布):","originalFile":"# The Bazaar Guide Site (大巴扎攻略站)\n\nA small CMS where streamers (up主) and invited writers in the Chinese-speaking\ncommunity of the card game The Bazaar publish written guides, so players can\nfind a build for a given hero and patch without scrubbing through videos.\n\n## Language\n\n### People\n\n**Admin** (管理员):\nOne of the few top streamers who run the site. Reviews and publishes other\npeople's Guides and manages users.\n_Avoid_: owner, superuser\n\n**Editor** (编辑):\nAn invited guide writer (another up主 or an experienced player). Writes\nGuides but cannot publish them or manage users.\n_Avoid_: author (as a role name), contributor, writer\n\n**Reader** (读者):\nAnyone who plays the game and reads the public site. Has no account.\n_Avoid_: user, visitor, member\n\n**Author** (作者):\nThe Admin or Editor who wrote a Guide. Readers can browse all of an Author's\nPublished Guides on that Author's page.\n_Avoid_: owner, creator, up主 (not every Author is a streamer)\n\n**Display name** (昵称):\nThe name an Author chooses to be shown under publicly. It is never their\nlogin username.\n_Avoid_: username, handle\n\n### Content\n\n**Guide** (攻略):\nA written strategy piece about one Hero on one Patch, typically built around\nscreenshots of a lineup or deck with an explanation of how it plays. Guides\nfor tournament mode are still Guides.\n_Avoid_: article, tutorial, post\n\n**Page** (页面):\nA standalone piece of site content written by an Admin, such as About (关于),\nthat appears in the public navigation.\n_Avoid_: static page\n\n**Tournament announcement** (锦标赛预告):\nAn Admin-written notice about an upcoming in-game Tournament.\n_Avoid_: event, news, post\n\n**Tournament recap** (锦标赛回顾):\nAn Admin-written account of a Tournament that has already happened. It is a\nseparate item from that Tournament's announcement.\n_Avoid_: event, report, result\n\n**Chinese text / English text** (中文版 / 英文版):\nThe two language versions of a Guide (or other content), each with its own\ntitle and body. Chinese is required. English is optional, and content without\nit does not appear on the English site.\n_Avoid_: translation, localization, body\n\n### The game\n\n**Game Term** (游戏术语):\nA named thing in The Bazaar that has an official Chinese name and an official\nEnglish name, stored as a pair. It is one of seven kinds: Hero, Item, Skill,\nEnchantment, Monster, Merchant, or Event.\n_Avoid_: keyword, tag, entity\n\n**Item** (物品):\nThe Game Term kind for the cards a player builds with.\n_Avoid_: card\n\n**Event** (事件):\nThe Game Term kind for an in-game event a player encounters during a run. The\nword means only this; it is never used for a Tournament.\n_Avoid_: using \"event\" for Tournaments or site activity\n\n**Hero** (英雄):\nThe Game Term for a playable character. Every Guide is about exactly one Hero.\n_Avoid_: character, class\n\n**Official name** (官方名称):\nThe name the game itself uses for a Game Term in a given language. The site\nonly ever shows Official names.\n_Avoid_: nickname (外号), alias, translation\n\n**Patch** (版本):\nThe game version a Guide was written for, such as `6.7`. Picked by the\nwriter. It describes when the Guide was written and is not a verdict on\nwhether the Guide is out of date.\n_Avoid_: version (also used for edits to a Guide), season\n\n**Current Patch** (当前版本):\nThe newest Patch of the game, as set by an Admin.\n_Avoid_: latest version, live patch\n\n**Tournament** (锦标赛):\nAn experimental in-game mode in which many players (up to about 100) play one\ngame together until there is one champion. It is run by the game, not\norganized by players. It has its own section on the site.\n_Avoid_: event, competition, league, match\n\n### Workflow\n\n**Draft** (草稿):\nA Guide its writer has not finished yet. Only its writer and Admins can see it.\n_Avoid_: unpublished\n\n**Submitted** (待审核):\nA Guide its writer has marked finished, waiting for an Admin to review it.\n_Avoid_: pending, draft, ready\n\n**Return** (退回):\nAn Admin's decision that a Submitted Guide is not ready. It goes back to its\nwriter as a Draft, with the Admin's notes.\n_Avoid_: reject, decline\n\n**Review note** (审核意见):\nPart of a Return: a passage quoted from the Guide together with the Admin's\nadvice on how to fix it.\n_Avoid_: comment (comments stay on Bilibili), feedback\n\n**Publish** (发布):\nAn Admin's approval of a Submitted Guide, which makes it Published. Publishing\ndoes not by itself change the public site.\n_Avoid_: approve, go live\n\n**Published** (已发布):\nA Guide an Admin has approved. It will appear on the public site after the\nnext Site build.\n_Avoid_: live, approved\n\n**Revision** (修订):\nA proposed change to a Published Guide. While it waits for review the\nPublished Guide stays on the site unchanged. Once published, it replaces the\nold content and the old content is not shown.\n_Avoid_: version, new version, edit\n\n**Site build** (更新网站):\nRegenerating the public site from everything that is Published, and putting it\nonline. This is the only step that changes what Readers see.\n_Avoid_: publish, deploy, export\n\n## Flagged ambiguities\n\n- \"Draft\" was being used for both an unfinished Guide and a finished one\n  awaiting review. Those are now **Draft** and **Submitted**.\n- \"Version\" can mean the game's Patch or an edit to a Guide. Use **Patch** for\n  the game and **Revision** for an edit.\n- \"Publish\" meant both an Admin's approval and regenerating the site. Approval\n  is **Publish**; regenerating is **Site build**. An Editor never publishes:\n  their button is Submit (提交审核).\n- \"Event\" is a Game Term kind (事件). Tournament items are announcements and\n  recaps, never \"events\".\n- \"Card\" and \"Item\" are the same thing. Use **Item**.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":127,"oldLines":6,"newStart":127,"newLines":11,"lines":[" does not by itself change the public site."," _Avoid_: approve, go live"," ","+**Unpublish** (撤下):","+An Admin taking a Published Guide off the site without deleting it. The Guide","+goes back to its Author as a Draft, optionally with Review notes.","+_Avoid_: hide, archive, take offline","+"," **Published** (已发布):"," A Guide an Admin has approved. It will appear on the public site after the"," next Site build."]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"39aa4973-4ffd-4aee-b1b5-99c37e774465","session_id":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"d1e69fc1-c6bd-41bf-a746-f18c4278d904","version":"2.1.288","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}

(file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"uuid":"e2f27cbb-2bc4-4390-9032-f4c5ba4c3ce8","timestamp":"2026-10-17T04:49:44.875Z","toolUseResult":{"filePath":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2/CONTEXT.md","oldString":"**Display name** (昵称):","newString":"**Submission ban** (禁止投稿):\nAn account state in which an Editor can still log in and work on Drafts but\ncannot Submit Guides or Revisions. Their Published Guides stay on the site.\n_Avoid_: suspension, block, mute\n\n**Deactivated** (已停用):\nAn account state in which the person cannot log in at all. Their Published\nGuides stay on the site.\n_Avoid_: deleted, disabled, banned\n\n**Display name** (昵称):","originalFile":"# The Bazaar Guide Site (大巴扎攻略站)\n\nA small CMS where streamers (up主) and invited writers in the Chinese-speaking\ncommunity of the card game The Bazaar publish written guides, so players can\nfind a build for a given hero and patch without scrubbing through videos.\n\n## Language\n\n### People\n\n**Admin** (管理员):\nOne of the few top streamers who run the site. Reviews and publishes other\npeople's Guides and manages users.\n_Avoid_: owner, superuser\n\n**Editor** (编辑):\nAn invited guide writer (another up主 or an experienced player). Writes\nGuides but cannot publish them or manage users.\n_Avoid_: author (as a role name), contributor, writer\n\n**Reader** (读者):\nAnyone who plays the game and reads the public site. Has no account.\n_Avoid_: user, visitor, member\n\n**Author** (作者):\nThe Admin or Editor who wrote a Guide. Readers can browse all of an Author's\nPublished Guides on that Author's page.\n_Avoid_: owner, creator, up主 (not every Author is a streamer)\n\n**Display name** (昵称):\nThe name an Author chooses to be shown under publicly. It is never their\nlogin username.\n_Avoid_: username, handle\n\n### Content\n\n**Guide** (攻略):\nA written strategy piece about one Hero on one Patch, typically built around\nscreenshots of a lineup or deck with an explanation of how it plays. Guides\nfor tournament mode are still Guides.\n_Avoid_: article, tutorial, post\n\n**Page** (页面):\nA standalone piece of site content written by an Admin, such as About (关于),\nthat appears in the public navigation.\n_Avoid_: static page\n\n**Tournament announcement** (锦标赛预告):\nAn Admin-written notice about an upcoming in-game Tournament.\n_Avoid_: event, news, post\n\n**Tournament recap** (锦标赛回顾):\nAn Admin-written account of a Tournament that has already happened. It is a\nseparate item from that Tournament's announcement.\n_Avoid_: event, report, result\n\n**Chinese text / English text** (中文版 / 英文版):\nThe two language versions of a Guide (or other content), each with its own\ntitle and body. Chinese is required. English is optional, and content without\nit does not appear on the English site.\n_Avoid_: translation, localization, body\n\n### The game\n\n**Game Term** (游戏术语):\nA named thing in The Bazaar that has an official Chinese name and an official\nEnglish name, stored as a pair. It is one of seven kinds: Hero, Item, Skill,\nEnchantment, Monster, Merchant, or Event.\n_Avoid_: keyword, tag, entity\n\n**Item** (物品):\nThe Game Term kind for the cards a player builds with.\n_Avoid_: card\n\n**Event** (事件):\nThe Game Term kind for an in-game event a player encounters during a run. The\nword means only this; it is never used for a Tournament.\n_Avoid_: using \"event\" for Tournaments or site activity\n\n**Hero** (英雄):\nThe Game Term for a playable character. Every Guide is about exactly one Hero.\n_Avoid_: character, class\n\n**Official name** (官方名称):\nThe name the game itself uses for a Game Term in a given language. The site\nonly ever shows Official names.\n_Avoid_: nickname (外号), alias, translation\n\n**Patch** (版本):\nThe game version a Guide was written for, such as `6.7`. Picked by the\nwriter. It describes when the Guide was written and is not a verdict on\nwhether the Guide is out of date.\n_Avoid_: version (also used for edits to a Guide), season\n\n**Current Patch** (当前版本):\nThe newest Patch of the game, as set by an Admin.\n_Avoid_: latest version, live patch\n\n**Tournament** (锦标赛):\nAn experimental in-game mode in which many players (up to about 100) play one\ngame together until there is one champion. It is run by the game, not\norganized by players. It has its own section on the site.\n_Avoid_: event, competition, league, match\n\n### Workflow\n\n**Draft** (草稿):\nA Guide its writer has not finished yet. Only its writer and Admins can see it.\n_Avoid_: unpublished\n\n**Submitted** (待审核):\nA Guide its writer has marked finished, waiting for an Admin to review it.\n_Avoid_: pending, draft, ready\n\n**Return** (退回):\nAn Admin's decision that a Submitted Guide is not ready. It goes back to its\nwriter as a Draft, with the Admin's notes.\n_Avoid_: reject, decline\n\n**Review note** (审核意见):\nPart of a Return: a passage quoted from the Guide together with the Admin's\nadvice on how to fix it.\n_Avoid_: comment (comments stay on Bilibili), feedback\n\n**Publish** (发布):\nAn Admin's approval of a Submitted Guide, which makes it Published. Publishing\ndoes not by itself change the public site.\n_Avoid_: approve, go live\n\n**Unpublish** (撤下):\nAn Admin taking a Published Guide off the site without deleting it. The Guide\ngoes back to its Author as a Draft, optionally with Review notes.\n_Avoid_: hide, archive, take offline\n\n**Published** (已发布):\nA Guide an Admin has approved. It will appear on the public site after the\nnext Site build.\n_Avoid_: live, approved\n\n**Revision** (修订):\nA proposed change to a Published Guide. While it waits for review the\nPublished Guide stays on the site unchanged. Once published, it replaces the\nold content and the old content is not shown.\n_Avoid_: version, new version, edit\n\n**Site build** (更新网站):\nRegenerating the public site from everything that is Published, and putting it\nonline. This is the only step that changes what Readers see.\n_Avoid_: publish, deploy, export\n\n## Flagged ambiguities\n\n- \"Draft\" was being used for both an unfinished Guide and a finished one\n  awaiting review. Those are now **Draft** and **Submitted**.\n- \"Version\" can mean the game's Patch or an edit to a Guide. Use **Patch** for\n  the game and **Revision** for an edit.\n- \"Publish\" meant both an Admin's approval and regenerating the site. Approval\n  is **Publish**; regenerating is **Site build**. An Editor never publishes:\n  their button is Submit (提交审核).\n- \"Event\" is a Game Term kind (事件). Tournament items are announcements and\n  recaps, never \"events\".\n- \"Card\" and \"Item\" are the same thing. Use **Item**.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":27,"oldLines":6,"newStart":27,"newLines":16,"lines":[" Published Guides on that Author's page."," _Avoid_: owner, creator, up主 (not every Author is a streamer)"," ","+**Submission ban** (禁止投稿):","+An account state in which an Editor can still log in and work on Drafts but","+cannot Submit Guides or Revisions. Their Published Guides stay on the site.","+_Avoid_: suspension, block, mute","+","+**Deactivated** (已停用):","+An account state in which the person cannot log in at all. Their Published","+Guides stay on the site.","+_Avoid_: deleted, disabled, banned","+"," **Display name** (昵称):"," The name an Author chooses to be shown under publicly. Only Admins can see it, and they can restore a Guide\nfrom it or delete it for good. A Guide in the Trash is never on the site.\n_Avoid_: archive, recycle bin, deleted\n\n**Revision** (修订):","originalFile":"# The Bazaar Guide Site (大巴扎攻略站)\n\nA small CMS where streamers (up主) and invited writers in the Chinese-speaking\ncommunity of the card game The Bazaar publish written guides, so players can\nfind a build for a given hero and patch without scrubbing through videos.\n\n## Language\n\n### People\n\n**Admin** (管理员):\nOne of the few top streamers who run the site. Reviews and publishes other\npeople's Guides and manages users.\n_Avoid_: owner, superuser\n\n**Editor** (编辑):\nAn invited guide writer (another up主 or an experienced player). Writes\nGuides but cannot publish them or manage users.\n_Avoid_: author (as a role name), contributor, writer\n\n**Reader** (读者):\nAnyone who plays the game and reads the public site. Has no account.\n_Avoid_: user, visitor, member\n\n**Author** (作者):\nThe Admin or Editor who wrote a Guide. Readers can browse all of an Author's\nPublished Guides on that Author's page.\n_Avoid_: owner, creator, up主 (not every Author is a streamer)\n\n**Submission ban** (禁止投稿):\nAn account state in which an Editor can still log in and work on Drafts but\ncannot Submit Guides or Revisions. Their Published Guides stay on the site.\n_Avoid_: suspension, block, mute\n\n**Deactivated** (已停用):\nAn account state in which the person cannot log in at all. Their Published\nGuides stay on the site.\n_Avoid_: deleted, disabled, banned\n\n**Display name** (昵称):\nThe name an Author chooses to be shown under publicly. It is never their\nlogin username.\n_Avoid_: username, handle\n\n### Content\n\n**Guide** (攻略):\nA written strategy piece about one Hero on one Patch, typically built around\nscreenshots of a lineup or deck with an explanation of how it plays. Guides\nfor tournament mode are still Guides.\n_Avoid_: article, tutorial, post\n\n**Page** (页面):\nA standalone piece of site content written by an Admin, such as About (关于),\nthat appears in the public navigation.\n_Avoid_: static page\n\n**Tournament announcement** (锦标赛预告):\nAn Admin-written notice about an upcoming in-game Tournament.\n_Avoid_: event, news, post\n\n**Tournament recap** (锦标赛回顾):\nAn Admin-written account of a Tournament that has already happened. It is a\nseparate item from that Tournament's announcement.\n_Avoid_: event, report, result\n\n**Chinese text / English text** (中文版 / 英文版):\nThe two language versions of a Guide (or other content), each with its own\ntitle and body. Chinese is required. English is optional, and content without\nit does not appear on the English site.\n_Avoid_: translation, localization, body\n\n### The game\n\n**Game Term** (游戏术语):\nA named thing in The Bazaar that has an official Chinese name and an official\nEnglish name, stored as a pair. It is one of seven kinds: Hero, Item, Skill,\nEnchantment, Monster, Merchant, or Event.\n_Avoid_: keyword, tag, entity\n\n**Item** (物品):\nThe Game Term kind for the cards a player builds with.\n_Avoid_: card\n\n**Event** (事件):\nThe Game Term kind for an in-game event a player encounters during a run. The\nword means only this; it is never used for a Tournament.\n_Avoid_: using \"event\" for Tournaments or site activity\n\n**Hero** (英雄):\nThe Game Term for a playable character. Every Guide is about exactly one Hero.\n_Avoid_: character, class\n\n**Official name** (官方名称):\nThe name the game itself uses for a Game Term in a given language. The site\nonly ever shows Official names.\n_Avoid_: nickname (外号), alias, translation\n\n**Patch** (版本):\nThe game version a Guide was written for, such as `6.7`. Picked by the\nwriter. It describes when the Guide was written and is not a verdict on\nwhether the Guide is out of date.\n_Avoid_: version (also used for edits to a Guide), season\n\n**Current Patch** (当前版本):\nThe newest Patch of the game, as set by an Admin.\n_Avoid_: latest version, live patch\n\n**Tournament** (锦标赛):\nAn experimental in-game mode in which many players (up to about 100) play one\ngame together until there is one champion. It is run by the game, not\norganized by players. It has its own section on the site.\n_Avoid_: event, competition, league, match\n\n### Workflow\n\n**Draft** (草稿):\nA Guide its writer has not finished yet. Only its writer and Admins can see it.\n_Avoid_: unpublished\n\n**Submitted** (待审核):\nA Guide its writer has marked finished, waiting for an Admin to review it.\n_Avoid_: pending, draft, ready\n\n**Return** (退回):\nAn Admin's decision that a Submitted Guide is not ready. It goes back to its\nwriter as a Draft, with the Admin's notes.\n_Avoid_: reject, decline\n\n**Review note** (审核意见):\nPart of a Return: a passage quoted from the Guide together with the Admin's\nadvice on how to fix it.\n_Avoid_: comment (comments stay on Bilibili), feedback\n\n**Publish** (发布):\nAn Admin's approval of a Submitted Guide, which makes it Published. Publishing\ndoes not by itself change the public site.\n_Avoid_: approve, go live\n\n**Unpublish** (撤下):\nAn Admin taking a Published Guide off the site without deleting it. The Guide\ngoes back to its Author as a Draft, optionally with Review notes.\n_Avoid_: hide, archive, take offline\n\n**Published** (已发布):\nA Guide an Admin has approved. It will appear on the public site after the\nnext Site build.\n_Avoid_: live, approved\n\n**Revision** (修订):\nA proposed change to a Published Guide. While it waits for review the\nPublished Guide stays on the site unchanged. Once published, it replaces the\nold content and the old content is not shown.\n_Avoid_: version, new version, edit\n\n**Site build** (更新网站):\nRegenerating the public site from everything that is Published, and putting it\nonline. This is the only step that changes what Readers see.\n_Avoid_: publish, deploy, export\n\n## Flagged ambiguities\n\n- \"Draft\" was being used for both an unfinished Guide and a finished one\n  awaiting review. Those are now **Draft** and **Submitted**.\n- \"Version\" can mean the game's Patch or an edit to a Guide. Use **Patch** for\n  the game and **Revision** for an edit.\n- \"Publish\" meant both an Admin's approval and regenerating the site. Approval\n  is **Publish**; regenerating is **Site build**. An Editor never publishes:\n  their button is Submit (提交审核).\n- \"Event\" is a Game Term kind (事件). Tournament items are announcements and\n  recaps, never \"events\".\n- \"Card\" and \"Item\" are the same thing. Use **Item**.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":147,"oldLines":6,"newStart":147,"newLines":11,"lines":[" next Site build."," _Avoid_: live, approved"," ","+**Trash** (回收站):","+Where deleted Guides go. {"parentUuid":"18d27b24-6ca7-451b-ab90-9eafcc758e54","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg7EmesuwKSMSqez9y11Q","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Nothing is left open. Please check this summary; if it's right, the next step is `/to-spec`.\n\n**What a \"post\" is.** Capability 3's posts are **Guides**. Each one has exactly one Hero, picked from the official list, and one Patch, picked from the Current Patch or the two before it. It has Chinese text (required) and English text (optional). Images are uploaded with alt text, and one of them is the cover. The URL is built from the hero's English name plus a number, like `guides/vanessa-12/`. Tournament-mode guides are still Guides.\n\n**What a \"page\" is.** **Pages** (such as About) are written by admins and show up in the navigation. The Tournaments section is a single newest-first list of admin-written **Tournament announcements** and **Tournament recaps**, each with a 预告 or 回顾 badge.\n\n**Who can do what:**\n- **Editors** can write, save Drafts, Submit, open Revisions on their own Published guides, upload images, and delete their own guides (deleted guides go to the Trash).\n- **Admins** can do everything editors can, on any guide. They also Publish, Return guides with Review notes (a quoted passage plus advice), Unpublish, edit Published guides directly, and restore guides from the Trash. They manage Pages, tournament items, Game Terms (CSV import, both official names required, a nickname list) and Patches. On the Users page they create accounts, change roles, apply a Submission ban, deactivate and reactivate accounts, and reset passwords. Admins can't remove themselves, and the last admin can't be removed.\n\n**What publishing means:**\n- **Publish** is an admin approving a guide.\n- A **Site build** (the 更新网站 button, or `cms publish`) is the only step that changes what Readers see.\n- An open **Revision** leaves the live guide up until it's approved, and then replaces it. No revision history is kept.\n\n**The public site:**\n- Chinese and English versions, switched from the top right.\n- Each item appears only in the languages it has.\n- Hero pages group guides by Patch, newest first.\n- Every Author with at least one Published guide gets an author page, shown under their Display name.\n- The header shows the Current Patch, and guides never get an \"outdated\" label.\n- `[[Game Term]]` markers show the official name in the reader's language.\n\n**Stretch tickets:**\n- **Image uploads with alt text.** You need this for your client, but it's also a rubric stretch item.\n- **A hosted admin console, as the last ticket.** At that point I write ADR-003 and we update `CLAUDE.md`. Until then, the \"never on the public internet\" rule still applies.\n\n**Out of scope:** comments, reader accounts, search, translation inside the CMS, a card database or patch notes, scheduled publishing, revision history, multi-site, drag-and-drop builders, and WYSIWYG editors.\n\n**Known gap until the hosted console exists:** the console runs on one machine, so editors on their own computers can't reach it.\n\nAll the vocabulary is in `CONTEXT.md`. The spec should note that capability 3's \"posts\" are Guides here. I didn't write any new ADRs. The one decision that would deserve one, hosting the console, gets ADR-003 when that ticket starts. `CONTEXT.md` isn't committed yet."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":56,"cache_read_input_tokens":98300,"output_tokens":1394,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":308},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":56,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1394,"cache_read_input_tokens":98300,"cache_creation_input_tokens":56,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":56},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011Cg7EmeRdPpwDceSAWsCb1","type":"assistant","uuid":"f07e3294-f1da-40d8-a864-da6ac7a4df3b","timestamp":"2026-10-17T05:14:15.642Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"high","perTurnEffort":"high","session_id":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"d1e69fc1-c6bd-41bf-a746-f18c4278d904","version":"2.1.288","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}

{"parentUuid":"9c307df1-5261-435c-81a4-108143b5e873","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"2df758e7-8898-4914-857c-e4c25f38e069","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/yining/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/to-spec\n\nThis skill takes the current conversation context and codebase understanding and produces a spec. Do NOT interview the user; just synthesize what you already know.\n\nThe issue tracker and triage label vocabulary should have been provided to you. If not, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n1. Explore the repo to understand the current state of the codebase, if you haven't already. Use the project's domain glossary vocabulary throughout the spec, and respect any ADRs in the area you're touching.\n\n2. Sketch out the seams at which you're going to test the feature. Existing seams should be preferred to new ones. Use the highest seam possible. If new seams are needed, propose them at the highest point you can. The fewer seams across the codebase, the better - the ideal number is one.\n\nCheck with the user that these seams match their expectations.\n\n3. Write the spec using the template below, then publish it to the project issue tracker. Apply the `ready-for-agent` triage label - no need for additional triage.\n\n<spec-template>\n\n## Problem Statement\n\nThe problem that the user is facing, from the user's perspective.\n\n## Solution\n\nThe solution to the problem, from the user's perspective.\n\n## User Stories\n\nA LONG, numbered list of user stories. Each user story should be in the format of:\n\n1. As an <actor>, I want a <feature>, so that <benefit>\n\n<user-story-example>\n1. As a mobile bank customer, I want to see balance on my accounts, so that I can make better informed decisions about my spending\n</user-story-example>\n\nThis list of user stories should be extremely extensive and cover all aspects of the feature.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\nA list of implementation decisions that were made. This can include:\n\n- The modules that will be built/modified\n- The interfaces of those modules that will be modified\n- Technical clarifications from the developer\n- Architectural decisions\n- Schema changes\n- API contracts\n- Specific interactions\n\nDo NOT include specific file paths or code snippets. They may end up being outdated very quickly.\n\nException: if a prototype produced a snippet that encodes a decision more precisely than prose can (state machine, reducer, schema, type shape), inline it within the relevant decision and note briefly that it came from a prototype. Trim to the decision-rich parts, not a working demo, just the important bits.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\nA list of testing decisions that were made. Include:\n\n- A description of what makes a good test (only test external behavior, not implementation details)\n- Which modules will be tested\n- Prior art for the tests (i.e. similar types of tests in the codebase)\n\n## Out of Scope\n\nA description of the things that are out of scope for this spec.\n\n## Further Notes\n\nAny further notes about the feature.\n\n</spec-template>\n"}]},"isMeta":true,"turnCompanion":true,"uuid":"2d7b754a-be22-4eb6-956f-dd582f5cd8f2","timestamp":"2026-10-17T05:38:14.374Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"d1e69fc1-c6bd-41bf-a746-f18c4278d904","version":"2.1.288","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}

{"parentUuid":"53f5a22a-0c56-4700-8628-1812963e1464","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"2df758e7-8898-4914-857c-e4c25f38e069","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_016GHi1qfFEafeLp5wkU3EaC","type":"tool_result","content":"# Issue tracker: GitHub\n\nIssues and specs for this repo live as GitHub issues. Use the `gh` CLI for all operations.\n\n## Conventions\n\n- **Create an issue**: `gh issue create --title \"...\" --body \"...\"`. Use a heredoc for multi-line bodies.\n- **Read an issue**: `gh issue view <number> --comments`, filtering comments by `jq` and also fetching labels.\n- **List issues**: `gh issue list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,comments --jq '[.[] | {number, title, body, labels: [.labels[].name], comments: [.comments[].body]}]'` with appropriate `--label` and `--state` filters.\n- **Comment on an issue**: `gh issue comment <number> --body \"...\"`\n- **Apply / remove labels**: `gh issue edit <number> --add-label \"...\"` / `--remove-label \"...\"`\n- **Close**: `gh issue close <number> --comment \"...\"`\n\nInfer the repo from `git remote -v`; `gh` does this automatically when run inside a clone.\n\n## Pull requests as a triage surface\n\n**PRs as a request surface: no.** _(Set to `yes` if this repo treats external PRs as feature requests; `/triage` reads this flag.)_\n\nWhen set to `yes`, PRs run through the same labels and states as issues, using the `gh pr` equivalents:\n\n- **Read a PR**: `gh pr view <number> --comments` and `gh pr diff <number>` for the diff.\n- **List external PRs for triage**: `gh pr list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,author,authorAssociation,comments` then keep only `authorAssociation` of `CONTRIBUTOR`, `FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR`, or `NONE` (drop `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR`).\n- **Comment / label / close**: `gh pr comment`, `gh pr edit --add-label`/`--remove-label`, `gh pr close`.\n\nGitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs, so a bare `#42` may be either: resolve with `gh pr view 42` and fall back to `gh issue view 42`.\n\n## When a skill says \"publish to the issue tracker\"\n\nCreate a GitHub issue.\n\n## When a skill says \"fetch the relevant ticket\"\n\nRun `gh issue view <number> --comments`.\n\n## Wayfinding operations\n\nUsed by `/wayfinder`. The **map** is a single issue with **child** issues as tickets.\n\n- **Map**: a single issue labelled `wayfinder:map`, holding the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body. `gh issue create --label wayfinder:map`.\n- **Child ticket**: an issue linked to the map as a GitHub sub-issue (`gh api` on the sub-issues endpoint). Where sub-issues aren't enabled, add the child to a task list in the map body and put `Part of #<map>` at the top of the child body. Labels: `wayfinder:<type>` (`research`/`prototype`/`grilling`/`task`). Once claimed, the ticket is assigned to the driving dev.\n- **Blocking**: GitHub's **native issue dependencies**, the canonical, UI-visible representation. Add an edge with `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<child>/dependencies/blocked_by -F issue_id=<blocker-db-id>`, where `<blocker-db-id>` is the blocker's numeric **database id** (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq .id`, _not_ the `#number` or `node_id`). GitHub reports `issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by` (open blockers only, the live gate). Where dependencies aren't available, fall back to a `Blocked by: #<n>, #<n>` line at the top of the child body. Passwords come from the environment there; in\n# tests they are fixed and meaningless.\nDEMO_USERS = {\n    \"admin\": {\"email\": \"admin@example.test\", \"password\": \"test-admin-pw\"},\n    \"editor\": {\"email\": \"editor@example.test\", \"password\": \"test-editor-pw\"},\n}\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef client() -> TestClient:\n    return TestClient(create_app())\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef client_as():\n    \"\"\"Return a factory: client_as(\"editor\") -> a logged-in TestClient.\"\"\"\n\n    def _login(role: str) -> TestClient:\n        user = DEMO_USERS[role]\n        c = TestClient(create_app())\n        response = c.post(\"/login\", data={\"email\": user[\"email\"],\n                                          \"password\": user[\"password\"]},\n                          follow_redirects=False)\n        if response.status_code == 404:\n            pytest.skip(\"No /login route yet — build the login ticket first.\")\n        assert response.status_code in (200, 302, 303), (\n            f\"Login as {role} failed with {response.status_code}\")\n        return c\n\n    return _login\n\"\"\"T00: the walking skeleton. These pass in the fresh template.\n\nDo not delete them. As you build content types, extend this so it creates:\n  - one admin and one editor (passwords read from .env, never hard-coded)\n  - a few posts and pages, at least one draft and one published\n\nThe rubric expects this to run clean on a fresh clone with .env.example values\n(item E4), because the database itself is never committed.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\n\ndef main() -> int:\n    admin_pw = os.environ.get(\"CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD\")\n    editor_pw = os.environ.get(\"CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD\")\n    if not admin_pw or not editor_pw:\n        print(\"Set CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD and CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD in .env \"\n              \"(copy .env.example).\")\n        return 1\n\n    # If it says something you did not decide, fix it now — everything downstream inherits it.\n\n```text\n/to-tickets\n```\n\n**Expected:** 7–9 issues labeled `ticket`, each with acceptance criteria and its blocking edges. Aim for tickets that look like this:\n\n- ✅ **T03 — Editors can create and edit posts** (touches the model, a route, a template, and tests; demoable alone)\n- ❌ **T03 — Add all database models** (one layer only; nothing works until everything lands)\n\nThis is the **tracer bullet** idea: each ticket is a narrow but complete path through every layer, verifiable the moment it lands. If a ticket cannot be demoed by itself, split or merge it now — `/to-tickets` again with what you want changed.\n\nCheck your set on GitHub:\n\n```bash\ngh issue list --label ticket\n```\n\n### 6.3 The per-ticket runbook\n\nRepeat for each ticket, in blocking order. One ticket per fresh session.\n\n```text\n/clear\n/implement #3\n```\n\nClaude reads the ticket, the spec, and `CONTEXT.md`, then drives `/tdd`: a failing test first, then code, then a green test. **You never run pytest yourself.**\n\nWhen it is green:\n\n```text\n/code-review\n```\n\nIt reviews the change in a fresh subagent against the repo's standards and the spec.
