Where the course manual says **post**, this spec says **Guide**.\n\n## Problem Statement\n\nGuides for The Bazaar (大巴扎) in the Chinese-speaking community exist only as Bilibili videos and live streams. Most of them are an up主 talking over a PowerPoint. That fails the people who use them:\n\n- **Readers** can't read a guide in a few spare minutes, or when they can't turn the sound on. They can't jump straight to the end-game build (终局阵容) for a given Hero, and they can't tell whether a video still applies after a balance patch. Patches come about twice a month.\n- **Streamers and invited writers** already have the material (screenshots of lineups and decks, plus an explanation). They have nowhere to publish it as text, organized so a Reader can find it by Hero, Patch or Author.\n- **The streamers who would run a site** are good at managing fan groups but not comfortable with computers. They need a strict line between themselves and invited writers. Nothing reaches the public site until an Admin has reviewed it.\n\n## Solution\n\n**大巴扎攻略站** is a small CMS with an admin console and a static public site.\n\n- Editors write Guides in Markdown. Each Guide has exactly one Hero and one Patch, uploaded screenshots, and a Chinese text plus an optional English text.\n- Editors Submit Guides for review. Admins Publish them, or Return them with Review notes.\n- An Admin clicks **更新网站** (Site build) to regenerate the public site and put it on GitHub Pages.\n- Readers browse Guides by Hero (grouped by Patch, newest first) or by Author. They can switch the whole site between Chinese and English, and they see the Current Patch in the header.\n- Game names (Heroes, Items, Skills and the rest) always appear as the game's Official names, in the Reader's language.\n\n### The 7 required capabilities, for this client\n\n1. **Login.** Admins and Editors sign in with email and password, and sign out. Passwords are hashed with argon2 and never stored or logged in plain text. Deactivated accounts can't log in. An account created by an Admin starts with a temporary password, and on first login the person sets their own password and Display name.\n2. **Two roles.** **Admin** (管理员): a streamer who runs the site, reviews and Publishes everyone's Guides, and manages users, Pages, Tournament items, Game Terms and Patches. **Editor** (编辑): an invited writer who writes their own Guides and Submits them. An Editor can never Publish, Return, see other people's unpublished Guides, or manage users.\n3. **Posts = Guides.** Each Guide has full create, read, update and delete:\n   - **Fields:** a title and a Markdown body per language, a slug, a Hero, a Patch, a status (Draft / Submitted / Published), the Author, and timestamps.\n   - **Changing a Published Guide:** goes through a Revision, so the live Guide stays up until the change is approved.\n   - **Deleting:** sends the Guide to the Trash.\n4. **Pages.** Admins write Pages (About 关于) with the same fields minus Hero and Patch. Published Pages appear in the public navigation. Tournament announcements and recaps are a small Admin-only list under the 锦标赛 menu.\n5. **Admin console.** A role-aware dashboard with counts (待审核, Returned, my Drafts, changes not yet on the site) and a content list filterable by status, Hero, Author, Patch and language. The Markdown editor has a preview that shows the Guide as Readers will see it, with warnings for unknown Game Terms and nicknames.\n6. **User management (Admin only).** A Users page where Admins can:\n   - create accounts and change roles,\n   - apply or lift a Submission ban,\n   - deactivate or reactivate accounts,\n   - reset passwords.\n\n   Deactivated users can't log in. Admins can't deactivate or demote themselves, and the last active Admin can never be removed.\n7. **Public site and Site build.**\n   - Only Published content is written, with Markdown sanitized.\n   - The navigation is 攻略 and 锦标赛 plus the Published Pages.\n   - The site is built as Chinese and English versions with relative paths only.\n   - The Site build (`cms publish` plus deploy, or the 更新网站 button) is the only step that changes what Readers see.\n\n## User Stories\n\n### Accounts and login\n\n1. As an Admin, I want to sign in with my email and password, so that only I can use my Admin powers.\n2. As an Editor, I want to sign in with my email and password, so that I can work on my Guides.\n3. As an Admin or Editor, I want to sign out, so that nobody else at this computer can act as me.\n4. As an Admin, I want passwords stored only as argon2 hashes, so that a leaked database doesn't leak anyone's password.\n5. As a new Editor, I want to set my own password on first login, so that the temporary password the Admin chose stops working.\n6. As a new Editor, I want to choose my own Display name (my Bilibili name) on first login, so that Readers recognize me.\n7. As an Editor, I want to change my Display name later in my profile, so that I can follow a rename on Bilibili.\n8. As an Author, I want my Display name to be unique on the site, so that Readers never confuse me with another writer.\n9. As an Author, I want my login email never shown on the public site, so that strangers can't use it to try to log in as me.\n10. As a Deactivated user, I want a clear \"account deactivated\" message when I try to log in, so that I know to contact an Admin rather than retry.\n11. As an Admin, I want every form that changes something to carry a CSRF token, so that a malicious link can't act on my behalf.\n\n### Writing Guides\n\n12. As an Editor, I want to create a Guide with a Chinese title and Markdown body, so that I can turn my PowerPoint into a readable text.\n13. As an Editor, I want to optionally add an English title and body, so that English-speaking players can read my Guide too.\n14. As an Editor, I want to pick the Hero from a list of Official names, so that my Guide lands under the right Hero and never under a nickname.\n15. As an Editor, I want to pick the Patch from a list showing `6.7（当前版本）` and the two Patches before it, with the Current Patch preselected, so that I don't have to type or guess the version.\n16. As an Editor, I want to save a Draft and come back later, so that I can write a long Guide over several sittings.\n17. As an Editor, I want to upload screenshots of lineups and decks into my Guide, so that the pictures from my PowerPoint go straight into the text.\n18. As an Editor, I want to give each image an optional short description (alt text), so that Readers using screen readers, or whose images fail to load, still know what the picture shows.\n19. As an Editor, I want to choose which uploaded image is the Guide's cover, defaulting to the first, so that my Guide looks right in the lists.\n20. As an Editor, I want to use one uploaded image in both my Chinese and my English text, so that I don't upload it twice.\n21. As an Editor, I want to mark a Game Term in my text as `[[瓦妮莎]]` or `[[Vanessa]]`, so that it shows as the Official name in whichever language the Reader is using.\n22. As an Editor, I want the preview to warn me about a `[[…]]` that matches no Game Term, so that I can fix typos before an Admin sees them.\n23. As an Editor, I want the preview to warn me when I've used a known nickname (such as 瓦姐) unmarked, so that I can replace it with the Official name.\n24. As an Editor, I want the preview to show my Guide as Readers will see it, so that I know the screenshots and layout come out right.\n25. As an Editor, I want to Submit (提交审核) a finished Guide, so that it goes to the Admins' review queue.\n26. As an Editor, I want to be stopped from Submitting a Guide with no Chinese text, so that I don't send something that can't be Published.\n27. As an Editor, I want the Submit button never to be labelled 发布, so that I'm not misled into thinking my Guide is live.\n28. As an Editor, I want to see only my own Guides in the console, so that the list is about my work.\n29. As an Editor, I want to edit my own Draft and Submitted Guides, so that I can fix something I noticed after Submitting.\n\n### Review\n\n30. As an Admin, I want a 待审核 count and queue on my dashboard, so that I never forget Guides waiting for me.\n31. As an Admin, I want to read a Submitted Guide in the same preview Readers will get, so that I review exactly what would be Published.\n32. As an Admin, I want to Publish a Submitted Guide, so that it goes on the site at the next Site build.\n33. As an Admin, I want to Return a Submitted Guide with one or more Review notes, each quoting a passage and giving advice, so that the Editor knows exactly what to fix and why.\n34. As an Editor, I want a badge on my dashboard when a Guide is Returned, so that I notice it without checking every Guide.\n35. As an Editor, I want to see the Review notes at the top of my Returned Draft, with quoted passages that are still in the text highlighted in the preview, so that I can find each problem quickly.\n36. As an Editor, I want to fix a Returned Guide and Submit it again, so that it can still be Published.\n37. As an Admin, I want earlier Review notes kept with the Guide, so that I can see its history if it goes back and forth.\n38. As an Admin, I want to fix small things myself and Publish directly, so that a typo doesn't cost a full round trip.\n39. As an Admin, I want to change any Guide's Hero, so that I can fix a Guide filed under the wrong Hero.\n40. As an Admin, I want to write and Publish my own Guides without review, so that streamers who run the site aren't slowed down.\n\n### Revisions, Unpublish, deletion\n\n41. As an Editor, I want to open a Revision on my Published Guide, so that I can update it for a new Patch while the old version stays on the site.\n42. As an Editor, I want to save a Revision as a Draft and Submit it later, so that a big update can take several sittings.\n43. As an Editor, I want my Revision to be able to change the Patch, so that a 6.7 Guide updated for 6.8 moves to the 6.8 group on its Hero's page.\n44. As an Editor, I want an approved Revision to replace the old content completely, so that Readers only ever see the current version.\n45. As an Admin, I want to Publish or Return a Revision just like a new Guide, so that review works the same either way.\n46. As an Editor, I want a Returned Revision to leave my live Guide untouched, so that a rejected update never takes my Guide down.\n47. As an Editor, I want at most one open Revision per Guide, so that there's never confusion about which change is pending.\n48. As an Admin, I want my own edits to a Published Guide to take effect immediately, so that I don't have to review myself.\n49. As a Reader, I want to see when a Guide was last updated (更新于), so that I can judge how fresh it is.\n50. As an Admin, I want to Unpublish (撤下) a Guide with an optional Review note, so that I can take down a misleading Guide without destroying the Author's work.\n51. As an Editor, I want an Unpublished Guide to come back to me as a Draft, so that I can fix it and Submit again.\n52. As an Editor, I want to delete my own Guides, including Published ones, so that I stay in control of my work.\n53. As an Editor, I want a confirmation before deleting, so that a misclick doesn't remove a Guide.\n54. As an Admin, I want deleted Guides to go to a Trash only Admins can see, so that an accidental deletion can be undone.\n55. As an Admin, I want to restore a Guide from the Trash, so that it returns to its Author in the state it was in.\n56. As an Admin, I want to delete a Guide from the Trash for good, together with its images, so that the Trash doesn't grow forever.\n57. As an Admin, I want any Guide in the Trash never to appear on the site, so that deleting a Guide always takes it down at the next Site build.\n\n### Game Terms and Patches\n\n58. As an Admin, I want to manage Game Terms of seven kinds (Hero, Item, Skill, Enchantment, Monster, Merchant, Event), each with its official Chinese and English name, so that the site always uses Official names.\n59. As an Admin, I want to import Game Terms from a CSV file, so that thousands of Items and Skills don't have to be typed by hand.\n60. As an Admin, I want CSV rows missing either Official name rejected with a clear per-row message, so that half-filled terms never get in.\n61. As an Admin, I want to see what an import will add or change before it is saved, so that a bad CSV doesn't corrupt the term list.\n62. As an Admin, I want to record known nicknames against a Game Term, so that the editor preview can warn Editors who use them.\n63. As an Admin, I want each Hero to have a URL slug derived from its English Official name, so that Hero pages have clean addresses.\n64. As an Admin, I want to add a new Patch, which becomes the Current Patch, so that a balance patch takes one action on my side.\n65. As a Reader, I want the Current Patch shown in the site header, so that I can compare it with each Guide's Patch myself.\n66. As a Reader, I want no automatic \"outdated\" labels, so that a Guide written for 6.6 that is still valid isn't wrongly flagged.\n\n### Pages and Tournaments\n\n67. As an Admin, I want to write an About (关于) Page with a Chinese and an optional English version, so that Readers know who runs the site and how to contact us.\n68. As an Admin, I want Published Pages to appear in the public navigation automatically, so that I don't have to edit menus by hand.\n69. As an Admin, I want to post a Tournament announcement with the Tournament's date, Patch and optional cover, so that Readers learn about an upcoming in-game Tournament.\n70. As an Admin, I want to post a Tournament recap as its own item, optionally linked to its announcement, so that past Tournaments stay on record.\n71. As a Reader, I want the 锦标赛 section to list announcements and recaps newest first, each badged 预告 or 回顾, so that I can tell at a glance what each item is.\n\n### User management\n\n72. As an Admin, I want a Users page listing every account's Display name, role, state, Guide counts and last login, so that I can see who's active.\n73. As an Admin, I want to create an Editor or Admin account with an email and temporary password, so that I can invite a writer.\n74. As an Admin, I want to change a user's role, so that I can promote a trusted Editor.\n75. As an Admin, I want to apply a Submission ban (禁止投稿) to an Editor, so that they can't Submit while their Published Guides stay up.\n76. As a banned Editor, I want to see why I can't Submit, so that I'm not confused by a missing button.\n77. As an Admin, I want to deactivate and reactivate accounts, so that someone who leaves can't log in but their Published Guides stay on the site.\n78. As an Admin, I want to reset a user's password to a new temporary one, so that a writer who forgot theirs can get back in.\n79. As an Admin, I want the console to stop me from deactivating or demoting myself, and from removing the last active Admin, so that the site can't be locked out.\n80. As an Editor, I want every user-management page to refuse me, even if I type its address, so that the role split is real and not just hidden buttons.\n\n### Dashboard and content list\n\n81. As an Admin, I want my dashboard to show 待审核, total Guides by status, and \"N 项更改尚未更新到网站\", so that I know what needs my attention.\n82. As an Editor, I want my dashboard to show my Drafts, my Submitted Guides and my Returned Guides, so that I know where my work stands.\n83. As an Admin, I want to filter the content list by status, Hero, Author, Patch and language, so that I can find any Guide quickly.\n84. As an Admin or Editor, I want a success or error message after every save, so that I'm never unsure whether something worked.\n85. As an Admin or Editor, I want a console navigation that stays on every page, so that I don't get lost the way I did in WordPress.\n86. As an Admin or Editor, I want every console label in Chinese, so that the tool feels like ours.\n\n### Site build and public site\n\n87. As an Admin, I want an 更新网站 button that runs the Site build and puts the site online, so that I never have to open a terminal.\n88. As an Admin, I want a clear message if the Site build fails, such as a failed push, so that I know the site didn't update.\n89. As a Reader, I want a home page showing the Current Patch, the newest Guides and a grid of Heroes, so that I can start browsing immediately.\n90. As a Reader, I want a page per Hero listing its Guides grouped by Patch, newest first, so that I can find a build for my Hero on this Patch.\n91. As a Reader, I want a page per Author listing all their Guides, so that I can follow writers I trust.\n92. As a Reader, I want list items to show the cover image, title, Hero, Patch, Author and date, so that I can choose a Guide without opening each one.\n93. As a Reader, I want a language switch at the top right that switches the whole site, so that I can read entirely in Chinese or entirely in English.\n94. As a Reader, I want switching language on a Guide to take me to the same Guide in the other language, or to its Hero's page with a notice if it isn't available, so that the switch never leads nowhere.\n95. As an English Reader, I want only Guides with English text listed on the English site, so that I never land on a page in a language I can't read.\n96. As a Reader, I want Hero and Author pages to exist in both languages, with a \"No English guides yet\" notice when empty, so that every link works.\n97. As a Reader, I want `[[Game Term]]` markers shown as the Official name in my language, so that Item and Skill names match what I see in game.\n98. As a Reader, I want Guide addresses that stay the same after a Revision, such as `guides/vanessa-12/`, so that links shared in Bilibili comments keep working.\n99. As a Reader, I want the site to work when served from a subfolder of GitHub Pages, so that every link and image loads.\n100. As an Admin, I want Drafts, Submitted Guides, open Revisions and the Trash never to appear on the site, so that only reviewed work is public.\n101. As a Reader, I want any script or unsafe HTML in a Guide stripped, so that a Guide can never attack my browser.\n\n### Stretch\n\n102. As an Admin, I want the console hosted somewhere Editors can reach from their own computers, behind the security gate (password from the environment, rate-limited login, HTTPS, no default accounts), so that writers across China can actually use it.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n**Modules**\n\n- **Accounts.** Users, login and logout, sessions (signed cookies via itsdangerous), argon2 hashing, CSRF tokens on every state-changing form, first-login setup (password plus Display name), and account states (active / Submission ban / Deactivated).\n  - Login is by email, matching the existing `client_as` test fixture. The Display name is separate, unique, and the only name shown publicly.\n  - Roles are bundles of capabilities. Route code checks a capability, not a role name, so a rule can change without touching routes.\n- **Guide workflow.** A deep module that owns every state change and its permission check: create, save, Submit, Publish, Return (with Review notes), Unpublish, open and Submit a Revision, delete to Trash, restore, delete for good. Its interface takes the acting user and the Guide, and either performs the change or refuses with a reason the console can show. No route changes Guide status directly.\n  - Guide states: Draft → Submitted → Published, with Return and Unpublish leading back to Draft. \"In Trash\" is separate from status, so a restored Guide comes back exactly as it was.\n  - A Revision is a pending copy of a Published Guide's editable fields (texts, Hero, Patch, images, cover), with its own Draft/Submitted state. There is at most one per Guide. Publishing it overwrites the Guide's fields and updates its timestamp. The old content isn't kept. Returning it leaves the Guide untouched.\n  - Admin edits to a Published Guide apply directly with no Revision.\n  - Submit requires Chinese text and is refused under a Submission ban.\n  - Review notes belong to the Guide and each stores a quoted passage, the advice, the Admin, and the time. They are kept across rounds.\n- **Content.**\n  - Guides have per-language title and body (Chinese required to Submit, English optional), a Hero, a Patch, the Author, a cover image, and created/updated/published timestamps.\n  - Pages have per-language text, a status (Draft/Published) and an Admin-set ASCII slug. Only Admins can manage them, with no review.\n  - Tournament items are of kind announcement or recap, with per-language text, a Tournament date, a Patch, an optional cover, an optional link from recap to announcement, and a Draft/Published status. Only Admins can manage them.\n- **Game Terms and Patches.**\n  - **Game Terms:** each has one of the seven kinds, both Official names (both required), and an optional list of nicknames. Heroes also have a URL slug from the English name.\n  - **CSV import:** uses Python's standard library, previews the changes, and rejects rows per row with a reason.\n  - **Patches:** a Patch is an ordered list entry, and the newest one is the Current Patch. The Guide form offers the Current Patch and the two before it, and still shows a Guide's existing older Patch.\n- **Markdown rendering.** One function used by both the editor preview and the Site build:\n  1. Markdown is turned into HTML with markdown-it-py.\n  2. `[[term]]` markers become the Official name in the target language, matched by either language's name, and styled as a term.\n  3. The HTML is sanitized with nh3.\n\n  The same pass returns warnings (unknown terms, unmarked nicknames) for the preview. Warnings never block Submit. Review notes' quoted passages are highlighted in the preview only, never on the public site.\n- **Media.**\n  - **Accepted files:** PNG, JPG, WebP and GIF only (no SVG), checked by content as well as extension. 5 MB maximum each.\n  - **Storage:** server-generated filenames. Images are owned by a Guide (or a Tournament item) and usable from either language's text. Each image has optional per-language alt text.\n  - **Site build and deletion:** images are copied into the site output during the Site build, and deleted with their owner when it is deleted for good.\n- **Site build.** It is an extension of the existing `render_site(out)`.\n  - **Output:** two trees, `zh/` and `en/`. The root `index.html` sends Readers to `zh/`.\n  - **Pages written per language:** the home page, a Guides index, one page per Hero, one per Author with at least one Published Guide, one per Guide, the Tournaments list and each item, and each Published Page.\n  - **Language filter:** the English tree includes only items with English text. Hero and Author pages exist in both trees, with an empty notice when needed.\n  - **Links:** every link is relative, computed from each page's depth. The language switch links to the same page in the other tree, or falls back to the Hero page with a notice.\n  - **What is excluded:** only Published, non-Trash content is read, so open Revisions are never seen.\n  - **Deploy:** the existing `cms deploy` (ghp-import) puts the site online. The console's 更新网站 button runs render plus deploy and shows the result. The CLI commands stay as they are.\n  - The dashboard's \"changes not yet on the site\" count compares content change times with the last successful Site build.\n- **URLs.**\n  - **Guides:** `guides/<hero-slug>-<id>/`. The slug is generated on creation, Admins can edit it, and it is unique. It never changes on its own with a title or Revision.\n  - **Other pages:** Heroes `heroes/<slug>/`, Authors `authors/<id>/` (never the email), Tournament items `tournaments/<id>/`, Pages `<page-slug>/`.\n- **Admin console.** Server-rendered Jinja templates with Chinese labels throughout:\n  - a role-aware dashboard,\n  - the filterable content list,\n  - the Guide editor with preview, image upload, cover choice and alt text,\n  - a review screen with a Review note builder,\n  - the Users page, the Trash, Game Terms with CSV import, and Patches.\n\n  Navigation stays on every page, and every save shows a success or error message.\n- **Storage.** SQLite at `CMS_DATABASE`. The schema is created on startup. `scripts/seed_demo.py` creates one Admin and one Editor from environment passwords, plus demo Heroes, Patches, Game Terms, Guides in every status, a Page and Tournament items.\n- **Architecture.** ADR-001 and ADR-002 stand for all core work. The hosted console is a stretch ticket. When it starts, ADR-003 will supersede ADR-001 for the console, and the `CLAUDE.md` \"never on the public internet\" rule will be updated in the same change. Until then the console runs on one machine. That is a known gap for a real multi-author deployment.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- **A good test** drives the system the way a user does and checks what a user would see: an HTTP response, a redirect, a page's text, or a file in the built site. Tests never inspect database rows or call private helpers, so the internals can be rebuilt without rewriting tests. Test names use the `CONTEXT.md` vocabulary (e.g. `test_editor_cannot_publish_a_submitted_guide`).\n- **Seam 1: the admin console over HTTP.** This uses the existing `client` and `client_as(role)` fixtures. It covers login and logout, account states, CSRF rejection, every permission rule (including Editors refused on Admin routes by URL), the full Guide workflow, Revisions, Review notes, Trash, Submission bans, user management guards, Game Term CSV import, Patch handling, image upload validation, and preview warnings.\n- **Seam 2: the Site build.** This uses the existing `render_site(out)` into a temporary folder, after content is set up through Seam 1. It covers:\n  - Published-only output: no Drafts, Submitted Guides, open Revisions or Trash.\n  - Relative paths only, across every generated page.\n  - Sanitized Markdown: injected script is stripped.\n  - `[[term]]` rendering per language.\n  - The English tree excluding Chinese-only items.\n  - Hero pages grouped by Patch.\n  - Author pages using Display names only.\n  - Navigation built from Published Pages.\n  - Images copied, with alt text.\n- **Isolation.** Each test gets a fresh SQLite database through `CMS_DATABASE` in a temporary folder, seeded with the `DEMO_USERS` from the test fixtures.\n- **Prior art:** `tests/test_t00.py` (HTTP and `render_site` checks, the relative-path assertion) and `tests/conftest.py` (`client_as`). The T00 tests must keep passing.\n- **Deploy** (the git push) isn't tested automatically. The button's handling of success and failure is tested with the push step replaced.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\n- Comments and discussion. These stay on Bilibili.\n- Reader accounts.\n- Site search. Browsing by Hero, Author and Patch covers the need on a static site.\n- Translation inside the CMS (machine or AI). Writers bring their own English text.\n- A card database or patch-notes section. The community wiki already covers it.\n- Automatic \"outdated\" labels on Guides.\n- Revision history and rollback. An approved Revision replaces the old content.\n- Scheduled publishing.\n- Streamer announcements as a content type.\n- Multi-site, drag-and-drop page builders, and WYSIWYG editors (excluded by the manual).\n- Hosting the console in core. It is the last stretch ticket only.\n\n## Further Notes\n\n- **Stretch tickets planned:** (1) image uploads with alt text, which the client needs and the rubric counts as \"Media uploads with alt text\"; (2) the hosted admin console behind the security gate, done last, with ADR-003.\n- **Known gap until the hosted console exists:** Editors on their own computers can't reach a console running on one Admin's machine. In the meantime every feature is built as if the console were shared: real logins, roles, CSRF, and no default accounts.\n- Because of ADR-001, Publishing doesn't change the public site by itself. The console says so wherever it matters (\"will appear after 更新网站\").\n- Client sources: `notes/client-brief.md`, `notes/cms-field-notes.md`, `notes/research-cms-vocabulary.md`, and the grill session recorded in `CONTEXT.md`.\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"e2201fc0-acb9-4d06-b02b-05552d6a3db6","session_id":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"d1e69fc1-c6bd-41bf-a746-f18c4278d904","version":"2.1.288","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}

{"parentUuid":"465a532a-2995-4f33-8342-09a61d01fb2c","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"1995a9b1-b989-47b9-8e4b-2d06a6df68e0","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/yining/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/to-tickets\n\n# To Tickets\n\nBreak a plan, spec, or conversation into a set of **tickets**: tracer-bullet vertical slices, each declaring the tickets that **block** it.\n\nThe issue tracker and triage label vocabulary should have been provided to you. If not, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Gather context\n\nWork from whatever is already in the conversation context. If the user passes a reference (a spec path, an issue number or URL) as an argument, fetch it and read its full body and comments.\n\n### 2. Explore the codebase (optional)\n\nIf you have not already explored the codebase, do so to understand the current state of the code. Ticket titles and descriptions should use the project's domain glossary vocabulary, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.\n\nLook for opportunities to prefactor the code to make the implementation easier. \"Make the change easy, then make the easy change.\"\n\n### 3. Draft vertical slices\n\nBreak the work into **tracer bullet** tickets.\n\n<vertical-slice-rules>\n\n- Each slice cuts a narrow but COMPLETE path through every layer (schema, API, UI, tests): vertical, NOT a horizontal slice of one layer\n- A completed slice is demoable or verifiable on its own\n- Each slice is sized to fit in a single fresh context window\n- Any prefactoring should be done first\n\n</vertical-slice-rules>\n\nGive each ticket its **blocking edges**: the other tickets that must complete before it can start. A ticket with no blockers can start immediately.\n\n**Wide refactors are the exception to vertical slicing.** A **wide refactor** is one mechanical change (rename a column, retype a shared symbol) whose **blast radius** fans across the whole codebase, so a single edit breaks thousands of call sites at once and no vertical slice can land green. Don't force it into a tracer bullet; sequence it as **expand–contract**. First expand: add the new form beside the old so nothing breaks. Then migrate the call sites over in batches sized by blast radius (per package, per directory), each batch its own ticket blocked by the expand, keeping CI green batch to batch because the old form still exists. Finally contract: delete the old form once no caller remains, in a ticket blocked by every migrate batch. When even the batches can't stay green alone, keep the sequence but let them share an integration branch that all block a final integrate-and-verify ticket; green is promised only there.\n\n### 4. Quiz the user\n\nPresent the proposed breakdown as a numbered list. For each ticket, show:\n\n- **Title**: short descriptive name\n- **Blocked by**: which other tickets (if any) must complete first\n- **What it delivers**: the end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work\n\nAsk the user:\n\n- Does the granularity feel right? (too coarse / too fine)\n- Are the blocking edges correct: does each ticket only depend on tickets that genuinely gate it?\n- Should any tickets be merged or split further?\n\nIterate until the user approves the breakdown.\n\n### 5. Publish the tickets to the configured tracker\n\nPublish the approved tickets. **How** depends on the tracker `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` configured; the tickets are the same either way, only the shape of the blocking edges changes:\n\n- **Local files** → write one file per ticket under `.scratch/<feature-slug>/issues/<NN>-<slug>.md`, numbered from `01` in dependency order (blockers first). Each file's \"Blocked by\" lists the numbers/titles it depends on. Use the per-ticket file template below: one ticket per file, never a single combined file.\n- **A real issue tracker (GitHub, Linear, …)** → publish one issue per ticket in dependency order (blockers first) so each ticket's blocking edges can reference real identifiers. Use the platform's native blocking / sub-issue relationship where it has one; otherwise set each ticket's \"Blocked by\" to the blocking issues. Apply the `ready-for-agent` triage label unless instructed otherwise; the tickets are agent-grabbable by construction.\n\nWork the **frontier**: any ticket whose blockers are all done. For a purely linear chain that means top to bottom.\n\nDo NOT close or modify any parent issue.\n\n<local-ticket-template>\n\n# <NN>: <Ticket title>\n\n**What to build:** the end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work, from the user's perspective, not a layer-by-layer implementation list.\n\n**Blocked by:** the numbers/titles of the tickets that gate this one, or \"None (can start immediately)\".\n\n**Status:** ready-for-agent\n\n- [ ] Acceptance criterion 1\n- [ ] Acceptance criterion 2\n\n</local-ticket-template>\n\n<issue-template>\n\n## Parent\n\nA reference to the parent issue on the tracker (if the source was an existing issue, otherwise omit this section).\n\n## What to build\n\nThe end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work, from the user's perspective, not layer-by-layer implementation.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] Criterion 1\n- [ ] Criterion 2\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- A reference to each blocking ticket, or \"None (can start immediately)\".\n\n</issue-template>\n\nIn either form, avoid specific file paths or code snippets: they go stale fast. {"parentUuid":"e4a1cb64-c54d-4de8-97a0-723c63480cab","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg7LUutGxGZwHDgzVXrVn","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I've broken the spec into 9 core tickets, which is the most the rubric's S1.5 allows (7–9 `ticket` issues), plus 2 `stretch` tickets. Each ticket is a vertical slice through model, route, template and tests.\n\n**Core (`ticket`)**\n\n1. **T01: Admins and Editors sign in and out**\n   - **Blocked by:** none\n   - **Delivers:** email and password login and logout, argon2 hashing, session cookies, and CSRF tokens on every form. The seed script creates one Admin and one Editor from environment passwords. On first login a user sets their own password and Display name. The console gets a persistent navigation bar and success/error messages. Every console page except login requires being signed in.\n   - **Note:** the T00 test expects `/admin` to answer \"hello admin\" without logging in. This ticket has to keep it passing, so the dashboard goes on a different route.\n2. **T02: Admins manage Heroes and Patches**\n   - **Blocked by:** T01\n   - **Delivers:** Admins add and edit Heroes (both Official names, with a slug from the English name). Adding a Patch makes it the Current Patch. Editors are refused.\n3. **T03: Editors write and Submit Guides; Admins Publish them**\n   - **Blocked by:** T02\n   - **Delivers:**\n     - Guide create and edit with Chinese text (required) and English text (optional), the Hero picker, and the Patch picker (Current Patch plus two older ones).\n     - The `guides/<hero>-<id>` slug, saving as Draft, Submit (提交审核), and Admin Publish. Admins' own Guides skip review.\n     - A preview with sanitized Markdown.\n     - The content list, filterable by status, Hero, Author, Patch and language. Editors see only their own Guides.\n     - Dashboard status counts.\n4. **T04: The Site build puts Published Guides online in Chinese and English**\n   - **Blocked by:** T03\n   - **Delivers:**\n     - `zh/` and `en/` trees: a home page (Current Patch, newest Guides, Hero grid), Guide pages, Hero pages grouped by Patch, and Author pages.\n     - The language switch with its fallback notice.\n     - Only Published content, relative paths only, and English-only filtering.\n     - The 更新网站 button (render plus deploy) with a result message, and the \"N 项更改尚未更新到网站\" count.\n5. **T05: Admins Return or Unpublish Guides with Review notes**\n   - **Blocked by:** T03\n   - **Delivers:**\n     - Return with one or more Review notes (a quoted passage plus advice), the Returned badge for the Editor, notes at the top of the Draft, quoted passages highlighted in the preview, and notes kept across rounds.\n     - Unpublish back to Draft.\n     - The 待审核 queue and count.\n6. **T06: Editors revise or delete their Published Guides**\n   - **Blocked by:** T04, T05\n   - **Delivers:**\n     - **Revisions:** at most one per Guide, with its own Draft/Submitted state, while the live Guide stays on the site. An approved Revision replaces the content (and can change the Patch). A Returned Revision leaves the live Guide untouched. Admin edits apply directly.\n     - **Deleting:** sends a Guide to the Trash, after a confirmation. Admins can restore it or delete it for good, and anything in the Trash never reaches the site.\n7. **T07: Game Terms with Official names in every Guide**\n   - **Blocked by:** T02, T04\n   - **Delivers:** all seven kinds, nicknames, and CSV import with a preview and rejection reasons per row. `[[term]]` markers render as the Official name in each language, both in the preview and on the site. The preview warns about unknown terms and unmarked nicknames.\n8. **T08: Pages and Tournament items appear in the public navigation**\n   - **Blocked by:** T04\n   - **Delivers:** Admin-written Pages (About) and Tournament announcements and recaps, each with its own Draft/Published status. The navigation is built from 攻略, 锦标赛 and the Published Pages. The 锦标赛 section is one list, newest first, with 预告/回顾 badges.\n9. **T09: Admins manage users**\n   - **Blocked by:** T03\n   - **Delivers:**\n     - The Users page: create accounts, change roles, Submission ban (Submit refused with a reason), deactivate and reactivate (deactivated users can't log in), and reset passwords.\n     - Admins can't deactivate or demote themselves, and the last active Admin can't be removed.\n     - Editors are refused on every Users route, even when typing the address.\n\n**Stretch (`stretch`)**\n\n- **S1: Image uploads with alt text and cover images**\n  - **Blocked by:** T04\n  - **Delivers:** PNG, JPG, WebP and GIF only, up to 5 MB, with server-generated filenames and alt text per language. The cover image appears in lists, and images are copied into the built site.\n- **S2: Hosted admin console behind the security gate**\n  - **Blocked by:** T01–T09 and S1\n  - **Delivers:** ADR-003 superseding ADR-001 for the console, an updated `CLAUDE.md` rule, rate-limited login, HTTPS, no default accounts, and the admin password from the environment.\n\nT04, T05, T07 and T08 can be worked in any order once their blockers close, but the per-ticket runbook takes one at a time.\n\n**Questions:**\n- **Granularity.** The biggest tickets are T03, T04 and T06. They had to be combined to stay within 9. Do any feel too large?\n- **Blocking edges.** Does T06 genuinely need T04? I put it there so \"the live Guide stays on the site while a Revision waits\" can be tested against a real build. The same goes for T07 needing T04 to render markers on the site.\n- **Images as stretch.** Images are central for your client, but the rubric counts \"media uploads with alt text\" as stretch, and stretch only counts once core is ≥70. {"parentUuid":"fb793c39-76e9-4753-a755-d7e91918a08a","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg7ZHEHVTEfrCpcm8ukhc","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01XARq3RpZA8ujC8Nbd5ar3i","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-yining-orca-workspaces-iphs400-mp2-cms-IPHS400-Mini-Project-2/d1e69fc1-c6bd-41bf-a746-f18c4278d904/scratchpad/tickets/T01.md","content":"## Parent\n\n#{{SPEC}}\n\n## What to build\n\nAdmins and Editors can sign in to the admin console with their email and password, and sign out. Passwords are stored only as argon2 hashes. Sessions use signed cookies, and every state-changing form carries a CSRF token.\n\nA fresh clone can be seeded with one Admin and one Editor whose passwords come from the environment. An account created with a temporary password makes its owner set a new password and a Display name on first login.\n\nThe console gets its shell: a persistent Chinese navigation bar, a success or error message after every save, and a dashboard that greets the signed-in user by Display name. Every console page except the login page requires being signed in.\n\nVocabulary: Admin, Editor, Display name, Deactivated (see `CONTEXT.md`).\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] An Admin and an Editor can each log in with email and password and land on the console dashboard.\n- [ ] A wrong password or unknown email is refused with the same message, so it doesn't reveal which accounts exist.\n- [ ] Logging out ends the session. Console pages then redirect to login.\n- [ ] Passwords are stored as argon2 hashes. No plain password appears in the database or logs.\n- [ ] A state-changing request without a valid CSRF token is rejected.\n- [ ] A user flagged for first-login setup must set a new password and a Display name before reaching any other console page.\n- [ ] Display names are unique. A duplicate is refused with a message.\n- [ ] A Deactivated user can't log in and sees an \"account deactivated\" message.\n- [ ] The seed script creates one Admin and one Editor from `CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD` and `CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD`, and refuses to run without them. There are no default passwords.\n- [ ] `client_as(\"admin\")` and `client_as(\"editor\")` work in tests.\n- [ ] The T00 tests still pass unchanged. {"parentUuid":"1a4d1a99-ebdc-4378-aeb9-27e7e3de99b2","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg7ZHEHVTEfrCpcm8ukhc","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01478bS9kNgxGDENJSuRwMN2","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-yining-orca-workspaces-iphs400-mp2-cms-IPHS400-Mini-Project-2/d1e69fc1-c6bd-41bf-a746-f18c4278d904/scratchpad/tickets/T03.md","content":"## Parent\n\n#{{SPEC}}\n\n## What to build\n\nAn Editor writes a Guide in Markdown and moves it through Draft → Submitted. An Admin Publishes it.\n\n**Writing a Guide**\n- A Guide has a Chinese title and body (required to Submit), an optional English title and body, one Hero, one Patch, an Author, and timestamps.\n- The Hero is picked from the Official names list.\n- The Patch is picked from a list showing the Current Patch (labelled `（当前版本）`, preselected) and the two Patches before it.\n- Each Guide gets a slug of the form `<hero-slug>-<id>`. An Admin can edit it, and it never changes on its own.\n\n**Workflow**\n- The Editor's button is **提交审核** (Submit), never 发布.\n- Admins Publish Submitted Guides. Admins' own Guides can be Published directly.\n- Admins can change any Guide's Hero.\n\n**Preview and console**\n- The editor has a preview that renders the Markdown, sanitized, as Readers will see it.\n- The console content list can be filtered by status, Hero, Author, Patch and language. Editors only ever see their own Guides.\n- The dashboard shows counts of Guides by status.\n\nAll status changes go through one Guide workflow module that checks permissions, as described in the spec.\n\nVocabulary: Guide, Draft, Submitted, Publish, Published, Author, Chinese text / English text.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] An Editor can create a Guide, save it as a Draft, and edit it later.\n- [ ] The Hero picker lists Official names only. The Patch picker offers the Current Patch (preselected and labelled current) plus the two previous Patches.\n- [ ] A new Guide gets a unique slug `<hero-slug>-<id>`. Editing the title doesn't change it. An Admin can change it, and a duplicate is refused.\n- [ ] An Editor can Submit their Draft. A Guide with no Chinese text can't be Submitted, and the console says why.\n- [ ] The Editor's submit control reads 提交审核 and nothing in the Editor's views offers 发布.\n- [ ] An Editor can't Publish a Guide, including by posting directly to the Publish route.\n- [ ] An Admin can Publish a Submitted Guide, and can create and Publish their own Guide without Submitting.\n- [ ] An Admin can change any Guide's Hero.\n- [ ] An Editor can't see or open another person's Guides.\n- [ ] The preview renders Markdown and strips `<script>` and other unsafe HTML.\n- [ ] The content list filters by status, Hero, Author, Patch and language.\n- [ ] The dashboard shows counts by status: an Editor sees their own, and an Admin sees all.\n- [ ] The seed script creates demo Guides in Draft, Submitted and Published.\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- #{{T02}}\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":684,"cache_read_input_tokens":132984,"output_tokens":9781,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":684,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":9781,"cache_read_input_tokens":132984,"cache_creation_input_tokens":684,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":684},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01478bS9kNgxGDENJSuRwMN2":{"file_path":"/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-yining-orca-workspaces-iphs400-mp2-cms-IPHS400-Mini-Project-2/d1e69fc1-c6bd-41bf-a746-f18c4278d904/scratchpad/tickets/T03.md","content":"## An Admin Publishes it.\n\n**Writing a Guide**\n- A Guide has a Chinese title and body (required to Submit), an optional English title and body, one Hero, one Patch, an Author, and timestamps.\n- The Hero is picked from the Official names list.\n- The Patch is picked from a list showing the Current Patch (labelled `（当前版本）`, preselected) and the two Patches before it.\n- Each Guide gets a slug of the form `<hero-slug>-<id>`. An Admin can edit it, and it never changes on its own.\n\n**Workflow**\n- The Editor's button is **提交审核** (Submit), never 发布.\n- Admins Publish Submitted Guides. Admins' own Guides can be Published directly.\n- Admins can change any Guide's Hero.\n\n**Preview and console**\n- The editor has a preview that renders the Markdown, sanitized, as Readers will see it.\n- The console content list can be filtered by status, Hero, Author, Patch and language. Editors only ever see their own Guides.\n- The dashboard shows counts of Guides by status.\n\nAll status changes go through one Guide workflow module that checks permissions, as described in the spec.\n\nVocabulary: Guide, Draft, Submitted, Publish, Published, Author, Chinese text / English text.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] An Editor can create a Guide, save it as a Draft, and edit it later.\n- [ ] The Hero picker lists Official names only. The Patch picker offers the Current Patch (preselected and labelled current) plus the two previous Patches.\n- [ ] A new Guide gets a unique slug `<hero-slug>-<id>`. Editing the title doesn't change it. An Admin can change it, and a duplicate is refused.\n- [ ] An Editor can Submit their Draft. A Guide with no Chinese text can't be Submitted, and the console says why.\n- [ ] The Editor's submit control reads 提交审核 and nothing in the Editor's views offers 发布.\n- [ ] An Editor can't Publish a Guide, including by posting directly to the Publish route.\n- [ ] An Admin can Publish a Submitted Guide, and can create and Publish their own Guide without Submitting.\n- [ ] An Admin can change any Guide's Hero.\n- [ ] An Editor can't see or open another person's Guides.\n- [ ] The preview renders Markdown and strips `<script>` and other unsafe HTML.\n- [ ] The content list filters by status, Hero, Author, Patch and language.\n- [ ] The dashboard shows counts by status: an Editor sees their own, and an Admin sees all.\n- [ ] The seed script creates demo Guides in Draft, Submitted and Published.\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- #{{T02}}\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"b55901ab-e761-4d54-9531-5f8afd6ff30c","session_id":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"d1e69fc1-c6bd-41bf-a746-f18c4278d904","version":"2.1.288","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}

{"parentUuid":"1b4993e8-6eee-4f81-b49a-f80813831115","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg7ZHEHVTEfrCpcm8ukhc","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01UjCXu8meN4GjWwek6QMeq1","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-yining-orca-workspaces-iphs400-mp2-cms-IPHS400-Mini-Project-2/d1e69fc1-c6bd-41bf-a746-f18c4278d904/scratchpad/tickets/T04.md","content":"## Parent\n\n#{{SPEC}}\n\n## What to build\n\nThe Site build turns everything Published into the public site, in Chinese and English, and an Admin can put it online from the console.\n\n**What gets written**\n- `zh/` and `en/` trees, with the root sending Readers to `zh/`.\n- In each language:\n  - a home page with the Current Patch, the newest Guides and a Hero grid;\n  - one page per Guide;\n  - one page per Hero, listing its Guides grouped by Patch, newest first;\n  - one page per Author with at least one Published Guide, under their Display name.\n- The header shows the Current Patch.\n- The English tree includes only Guides that have English text. Hero and Author pages exist in both languages, with a \"No English guides yet\" notice when empty.\n\n**Language switch**\n- A switch at the top right links to the same page in the other language.\n- If a Guide has no text in the other language, the switch links to its Hero's page there, with a notice.\n\n**Rules**\n- Every link is relative.\n- Only Published content is read.\n\n**Putting it online**\n- The console's **更新网站** button (Admin only) runs the Site build plus the existing deploy, and reports success or failure.\n- The dashboard shows \"N 项更改尚未更新到网站\" until the next successful Site build.\n\nVocabulary: Site build, Published, Current Patch, Reader, Author, Display name.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] `render_site` writes `zh/` and `en/` trees and a root `index.html` that sends Readers to `zh/`.\n- [ ] Each language has a home page with the Current Patch, the newest Guides and a Hero grid.\n- [ ] Each Published Guide has its own page at `guides/<slug>/` in every language it has text for.\n- [ ] Each Hero page lists its Published Guides grouped by Patch, newest Patch first.\n- [ ] Each Author with at least one Published Guide has a page listing their Guides, at `authors/<id>/`. The page shows the Display name and never the email.\n- [ ] Draft and Submitted Guides never appear anywhere in the output.\n- [ ] A Guide without English text doesn't appear in the English tree. Empty Hero and Author pages show the \"No English guides yet\" notice.\n- [ ] The language switch links to the same page in the other language. On a Chinese-only Guide it links to that Hero's English page, with a notice.\n- [ ] No generated file contains `href=\"/` or `src=\"/\"`.\n- [ ] Markdown in Guides is sanitized in the output: injected `<script>` doesn't survive.\n- [ ] The 更新网站 button is Admin only. It runs render plus deploy, and shows success or the failure message (tested with the deploy step replaced).\n- [ ] The dashboard's count of changes not yet on the site goes up after a Publish and back to zero after a successful Site build.\n- [ ] The T00 tests still pass.\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- #{{T03}}\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":684,"cache_read_input_tokens":132984,"output_tokens":9781,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":684,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":9781,"cache_read_input_tokens":132984,"cache_creation_input_tokens":684,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":684},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01UjCXu8meN4GjWwek6QMeq1":{"file_path":"/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-yining-orca-workspaces-iphs400-mp2-cms-IPHS400-Mini-Project-2/d1e69fc1-c6bd-41bf-a746-f18c4278d904/scratchpad/tickets/T04.md","content":"## Parent\n\n#{{SPEC}}\n\n## What to build\n\nThe Site build turns everything Published into the public site, in Chinese and English, and an Admin can put it online from the console.\n\n**What gets written**\n- `zh/` and `en/` trees, with the root sending Readers to `zh/`.\n- In each language:\n  - The Guide becomes a Draft again.\n- [ ] An Editor can't Return or Unpublish anything, including by posting directly to those routes.\n- [ ] The Author's dashboard shows a Returned badge with the number of Returned Guides.\n- [ ] Review notes appear at the top of the Returned Draft for its Author.\n- [ ] In the preview, a quoted passage that is still in the text is highlighted, and one that has since been removed isn't.\n- [ ] Review notes from earlier rounds are still visible after a second Return.\n- [ ] The Editor can fix a Returned Guide and Submit it again.\n- [ ] An Admin can Unpublish a Published Guide, optionally with a Review note. It returns to its Author as a Draft and is absent from the next Site build.\n- [ ] Admins see a 待审核 count and a queue listing every Submitted Guide.\n- [ ] Review notes and highlights never appear on the public site.\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- {"parentUuid":"8418ac3d-ab70-4f2c-9b91-fd8ec2474afd","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg7ZHEHVTEfrCpcm8ukhc","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_014cFhP21XtktuWrYnsXRsSL","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-yining-orca-workspaces-iphs400-mp2-cms-IPHS400-Mini-Project-2/d1e69fc1-c6bd-41bf-a746-f18c4278d904/scratchpad/tickets/T06.md","content":"## Parent\n\n#{{SPEC}}\n\n## What to build\n\nEditors stay in control of their Published Guides without ever putting unreviewed content on the site.\n\n**Revision (修订)**\n- An Editor can open a Revision on their Published Guide: a pending copy of its texts, Hero and Patch.\n- The Revision goes Draft → Submitted on its own, and there is at most one per Guide.\n- While it waits, the Published Guide stays on the site unchanged.\n- When an Admin Publishes the Revision, it replaces the Guide's content and updates its \"更新于\" date. The old content isn't kept.\n- When an Admin Returns it, the live Guide is untouched.\n- An Admin's own edits to a Published Guide apply directly.\n- A Revision can change the Patch. The Guide then moves to the new Patch group on its Hero's page.\n\n**Trash (回收站)**\n- An Editor can delete their own Guide (including a Published one) after a confirmation. It goes to the Trash.\n- Only Admins see the Trash, and they can restore a Guide from it or delete it for good.\n- A Guide in the Trash never appears on the site.\n\nVocabulary: Revision, Trash, Published, Return.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] An Editor can open a Revision on their own Published Guide, save it as a Draft, and Submit it.\n- [ ] Opening a second Revision on the same Guide is refused while one is open.\n- [ ] While a Revision is open, the Site build still shows the old Published content.\n- [ ] Publishing the Revision replaces the Guide's texts, Hero and Patch, and the next Site build shows only the new content and the new \"更新于\" date.\n- [ ] Returning the Revision with Review notes leaves the live Guide unchanged.\n- [ ] A Revision that changes the Patch moves the Guide to that Patch's group on the Hero page.\n- [ ] An Admin's edit to a Published Guide applies immediately, with no Revision.\n- [ ] The Guide's slug and URL stay the same through a Revision.\n- [ ] An Editor can delete their own Guide in any status, after a confirmation step. They can't delete anyone else's.\n- [ ] A deleted Guide is in the Trash, visible to Admins only, and absent from the next Site build.\n- [ ] An Admin can restore a Guide from the Trash, and it comes back exactly as it was.\n- [ ] An Admin can delete a Guide from the Trash for good.\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- #{{T04}}\n- #{{T05}}\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":684,"cache_read_input_tokens":132984,"output_tokens":9781,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":684,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":9781,"cache_read_input_tokens":132984,"cache_creation_input_tokens":684,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":684},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_014cFhP21XtktuWrYnsXRsSL":{"file_path":"/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-yining-orca-workspaces-iphs400-mp2-cms-IPHS400-Mini-Project-2/d1e69fc1-c6bd-41bf-a746-f18c4278d904/scratchpad/tickets/T06.md","content":"## Parent\n\n#{{SPEC}}\n\n## What to build\n\nEditors stay in control of their Published Guides without ever putting unreviewed content on the site.\n\n**Revision (修订)**\n- An Editor can open a Revision on their Published Guide: a pending copy of its texts, Hero and Patch.\n- The Revision goes Draft → Submitted on its own, and there is at most one per Guide.\n- While it waits, the Published Guide stays on the site unchanged.\n- When an Admin Publishes the Revision, it replaces the Guide's content and updates its \"更新于\" date. The old content isn't kept.\n- When an Admin Returns it, the live Guide is untouched.\n- An Admin's own edits to a Published Guide apply directly.\n- A Revision can change the Patch. The Guide then moves to the new Patch group on its Hero's page.\n\n**Trash (回收站)**\n- An Editor can delete their own Guide (including a Published one) after a confirmation. It goes to the Trash.\n- Only Admins see the Trash, and they can restore a Guide from it or delete it for good.\n- A Guide in the Trash never appears on the site.\n\nVocabulary: Revision, Trash, Published, Return.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] An Editor can open a Revision on their own Published Guide, save it as a Draft, and Submit it.\n- [ ] Opening a second Revision on the same Guide is refused while one is open.\n- [ ] While a Revision is open, the Site build still shows the old Published content.\n- [ ] Publishing the Revision replaces the Guide's texts, Hero and Patch, and the next Site build shows only the new content and the new \"更新于\" date.\n- [ ] Returning the Revision with Review notes leaves the live Guide unchanged.\n- [ ] A Revision that changes the Patch moves the Guide to that Patch's group on the Hero page.\n- [ ] An Admin's edit to a Published Guide applies immediately, with no Revision.\n- [ ] The Guide's slug and URL stay the same through a Revision.\n- [ ] An Editor can delete their own Guide in any status, after a confirmation step. They can't delete anyone else's.\n- [ ] A deleted Guide is in the Trash, visible to Admins only, and absent from the next Site build.\n- [ ] An Admin can restore a Guide from the Trash, and it comes back exactly as it was.\n- [ ] An Admin can delete a Guide from the Trash for good.\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- #{{T04}}\n- #{{T05}}\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"2ac62d09-d800-449b-abdf-70e9a77bd87f","session_id":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"d1e69fc1-c6bd-41bf-a746-f18c4278d904","version":"2.1.288","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}

{"parentUuid":"c6832691-6ea4-460f-87a8-0c7ecef14ef1","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg7ZHEHVTEfrCpcm8ukhc","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01Cm5eL71VxSokXWsW8yyreY","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-yining-orca-workspaces-iphs400-mp2-cms-IPHS400-Mini-Project-2/d1e69fc1-c6bd-41bf-a746-f18c4278d904/scratchpad/tickets/T07.md","content":"## Parent\n\n#{{SPEC}}\n\n## What to build\n\nEvery game name in a Guide shows as the game's Official name, in the Reader's language.\n\n**Game Terms**\n- Admins manage Game Terms of all seven kinds: Hero, Item, Skill, Enchantment, Monster, Merchant, Event.\n- Each term has both Official names, plus optional nicknames.\n- Admins can import Game Terms from a CSV file. They see a preview of what will be added or changed before saving, and rows missing either Official name are rejected, each with a reason.\n\n**Markers**\n- Writers mark a term in their text as `[[瓦妮莎]]` or `[[Vanessa]]`, matched by either language's name.\n- A marker renders as the Official name in the target language, styled as a term, both in the preview and in the Site build.\n- The preview warns about markers that match no term, and about known nicknames used without a marker.\n- Warnings never block Submit.\n\nVocabulary: Game Term, Official name, Item, Event (the Game Term kind, never a Tournament).\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] An Admin can add and edit Game Terms of each of the seven kinds, with both Official names required.\n- [ ] An Admin can record nicknames against a Game Term.\n- [ ] CSV import shows a preview of the rows to be added or changed before anything is saved.\n- [ ] A CSV row missing either Official name, or with an unknown kind, is rejected with its row number and reason. Valid rows still import.\n- [ ] Editors are refused on every Game Term and CSV route.\n- [ ] `[[瓦妮莎]]` in a Guide's English text renders as \"Vanessa\" on the English site, and `[[Vanessa]]` in the Chinese text renders as \"瓦妮莎\" on the Chinese site.\n- [ ] Markers render the same way in the editor preview.\n- [ ] A marker that matches no Game Term produces a preview warning naming it.\n- [ ] A recorded nickname used without a marker produces a preview warning that names the Official name.\n- [ ] A Guide with warnings can still be Submitted.\n- [ ] Rendered term names are still sanitized: a malicious term name can't inject HTML.\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- #{{T02}}\n- A recap can optionally link to the announcement it follows.\n- None of this goes through review, because only Admins write them.\n- **Navigation:** 攻略, 锦标赛, then every Published Page.\n- **The 锦标赛 section** is one list, newest first, each item badged 预告 or 回顾.\n\nThe same language rule as Guides applies: an item without English text isn't in the English tree.\n\nVocabulary: Page, Tournament, Tournament announcement, Tournament recap.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] An Admin can create, edit, Publish, unpublish and delete Pages.\n- [ ] A Page's slug must be ASCII and unique.\n- [ ] Published Pages appear in the public navigation of every generated page, after 攻略 and 锦标赛. Draft Pages don't.\n- [ ] An Admin can create, edit, Publish and delete Tournament announcements and recaps, each with a date and Patch.\n- [ ] A recap can link to an announcement, and the link appears on the recap's public page.\n- [ ] The 锦标赛 list is newest first, and every item shows a 预告 or 回顾 badge.\n- [ ] Draft Pages and Tournament items never appear in the Site build.\n- [ ] Pages and Tournament items without English text are absent from the English tree.\n- [ ] Editors are refused on every Page and Tournament route.\n- [ ] Page and Tournament Markdown is sanitized like Guides.\n- [ ] The seed script creates an About Page and one of each Tournament item.\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- {"parentUuid":"747a3161-1170-4f2e-bf95-b6995e10d5c2","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg7ZHEHVTEfrCpcm8ukhc","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01DdhiqLAdxQNQaoKHKLLcZM","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-yining-orca-workspaces-iphs400-mp2-cms-IPHS400-Mini-Project-2/d1e69fc1-c6bd-41bf-a746-f18c4278d904/scratchpad/tickets/T09.md","content":"## Parent\n\n#{{SPEC}}\n\n## What to build\n\nAdmins manage every account from a Users page, and Editors can't reach it.\n\n**The Users page** lists Display name, email, role, state (active / Submission ban / Deactivated), Guide counts, and last login. From it an Admin can:\n- create an account (email, role and temporary password; the user does first-login setup);\n- change a user's role;\n- apply or lift a Submission ban (禁止投稿);\n- deactivate or reactivate an account;\n- reset a password to a new temporary one.\n\n**Effects of account states**\n- A banned Editor can still log in and edit Drafts, but Submit and opening a Revision are refused, with the reason shown.\n- Deactivated users can't log in.\n- In both cases their Published Guides stay on the site.\n\n**Lockout guards**\n- An Admin can't deactivate or demote themselves.\n- The last active Admin can never be deactivated or demoted.\n\nVocabulary: Submission ban, Deactivated, Admin, Editor, Display name.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] The Users page lists every account with Display name, role, state, Guide counts and last login.\n- [ ] An Admin can create an account with a temporary password, and that user must complete first-login setup.\n- [ ] An Admin can change another user's role, and the change takes effect on that user's next request.\n- [ ] A Submission-banned Editor can log in and edit Drafts, but Submit is refused with a visible reason.\n- [ ] Lifting the ban restores Submit.\n- [ ] A Deactivated user can't log in. Reactivating restores login.\n- [ ] Published Guides of a banned or Deactivated user remain in the Site build.\n- [ ] An Admin can reset a user's password. The old password stops working and the user must complete first-login setup again.\n- [ ] An Admin can't deactivate or demote themselves.\n- [ ] The last active Admin can't be deactivated or demoted by anyone.\n- [ ] An Editor gets a redirect or 403 on every Users route, including by typing the URL or posting directly.\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- #{{T03}}\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":684,"cache_read_input_tokens":132984,"output_tokens":9781,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":684,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":9781,"cache_read_input_tokens":132984,"cache_creation_input_tokens":684,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":684},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01DdhiqLAdxQNQaoKHKLLcZM":{"file_path":"/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-yining-orca-workspaces-iphs400-mp2-cms-IPHS400-Mini-Project-2/d1e69fc1-c6bd-41bf-a746-f18c4278d904/scratchpad/tickets/T09.md","content":"## Parent\n\n#{{SPEC}}\n\n## What to build\n\nAdmins manage every account from a Users page, and Editors can't reach it.\n\n**The Users page** lists Display name, email, role, state (active / Submission ban / Deactivated), Guide counts, and last login. From it an Admin can:\n- create an account (email, role and temporary password; the user does first-login setup);\n- change a user's role;\n- apply or lift a Submission ban (禁止投稿);\n- deactivate or reactivate an account;\n- reset a password to a new temporary one.\n\n**Effects of account states**\n- A banned Editor can still log in and edit Drafts, but Submit and opening a Revision are refused, with the reason shown.\n- Deactivated users can't log in.\n- In both cases their Published Guides stay on the site.\n\n**Lockout guards**\n- An Admin can't deactivate or demote themselves.\n- The last active Admin can never be deactivated or demoted.\n\nVocabulary: Submission ban, Deactivated, Admin, Editor, Display name.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] The Users page lists every account with Display name, role, state, Guide counts and last login.\n- [ ] An Admin can create an account with a temporary password, and that user must complete first-login setup.\n- [ ] An Admin can change another user's role, and the change takes effect on that user's next request.\n- [ ] A Submission-banned Editor can log in and edit Drafts, but Submit is refused with a visible reason.\n- [ ] Lifting the ban restores Submit.\n- [ ] A Deactivated user can't log in. Reactivating restores login.\n- [ ] Published Guides of a banned or Deactivated user remain in the Site build.\n- [ ] An Admin can reset a user's password. The old password stops working and the user must complete first-login setup again.\n- [ ] An Admin can't deactivate or demote themselves.\n- [ ] The last active Admin can't be deactivated or demoted by anyone.\n- [ ] An Editor gets a redirect or 403 on every Users route, including by typing the URL or posting directly.\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- #{{T03}}\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"ea4260be-53f6-4fd5-9621-5f9fc8fd93b4","session_id":"aa9ac9da-70b0-4064-b175-26b8b3c5a4bf","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"d1e69fc1-c6bd-41bf-a746-f18c4278d904","version":"2.1.288","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}

{"parentUuid":"c15cc2a8-bb43-4530-ada7-2cdf486c6c30","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg7ZHEHVTEfrCpcm8ukhc","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01Ckmkgcjz2WDngV1NmePQrQ","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-yining-orca-workspaces-iphs400-mp2-cms-IPHS400-Mini-Project-2/d1e69fc1-c6bd-41bf-a746-f18c4278d904/scratchpad/tickets/S1.md","content":"## Parent\n\n#{{SPEC}}\n\n## What to build\n\nWriters upload the screenshots of their lineups and decks straight into a Guide. This counts toward the rubric's \"Media uploads with alt text\" stretch goal.\n\n**Uploads**\n- Only PNG, JPG, WebP and GIF are accepted, checked by file content and not just the extension. SVG is never accepted.\n- At most 5 MB per image.\n- Filenames are generated by the server.\n- Each image belongs to its Guide and can be used in both its Chinese and English text.\n- Each image has optional alt text per language.\n\n**Cover**\n- The writer picks a cover from the Guide's images, defaulting to the first. It shows in list items on the public site.\n\n**Site build and deletion**\n- The Site build copies the images into the site and references them with relative paths.\n- Deleting a Guide for good deletes its images.\n\nVocabulary: Guide, Author, Site build.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] An Editor can upload a PNG, JPG, WebP or GIF to their own Guide and insert it into either language's text.\n- [ ] An SVG, a non-image renamed to `.png`, and a file over 5 MB are each refused with a message.\n- [ ] Stored filenames are generated by the server, and an uploaded name like `../../x.png` can't escape the media folder.\n- [ ] Each image has optional Chinese and English alt text, used as the `alt` attribute on the matching language's page.\n- [ ] A Guide's cover defaults to its first image, and the writer can choose another.\n- [ ] Covers appear on home, Hero and Author list items in the Site build.\n- [ ] The Site build copies images into the output, with relative `src` paths only.\n- [ ] An Editor can't upload to or manage images on someone else's Guide.\n- [ ] Deleting a Guide from the Trash for good deletes its images.\n\n## Blocked by\n\n-
